Lin Ran quickly consoled her, "A household only needs one person who can cook—no need for a second. Besides, you work so hard to provide for us. Leave the kitchen to me."
Still, Lin Ran couldn’t figure it out. He’d watched Luo Yao’s every move—how did things still go wrong?
Was the poison not in the kitchen… but on Luo Yao herself?
Luo Yao gazed at Lin Ran with tender affection. "Ah Ran, I’m sorry. I’m not a good wife."
"Don’t you dare say that. If you’re not a good wife, then no one in this world is."
Uncle Fu adored watching Lin Ran and Luo Yao’s sweet daily interactions, though memories of the past made his heart ache slightly.
He side-eyed them and muttered inwardly, "Ohhh, if you’re not a good wife, then no one in this world is." (¬_¬)
Lin Ran and Luo Yao frowned in unison. "What’s with that look?"
Uncle Fu feigned innocence. "What look?"
"Your bonus for this month is revoked."
Uncle Fu: The sky has fallen.
Desperate, Uncle Fu shot Lin Ran a pleading glance, hoping he’d intercede like last time. But Lin Ran showed no intention of helping—in fact, he made it worse.
"Why are you looking at me? I have to listen to my wife."
Uncle Fu sighed deeply. This world truly had lost all meaning.
Luo Yao turned to Lin Ran. "Ah Ran, I want—"
"Alright, alright. You won’t stop until you break me, is that it?"
The next morning, Luo Yao went to Luo Corporation alone.
Why wasn’t Lin Ran with her? Because he hadn’t woken up yet.
As an ordinary man, he couldn’t keep up with Luo Yao’s adrenaline-fueled stamina.
The employees at Luo Corporation collectively sighed in relief when they saw Luo Yao arrive without Lin Ran.
Lately, they’d been force-fed so much "dog food" they were practically stuffed.
(Can’t find the book by title? Try searching the author—maybe it’s just been renamed!)
Lin Ran finally got to sleep in.
When he woke up, Luo Yao was already gone.
He called for Uncle Fu.
"Young Master Lin, you needed me?"
"Where’s my wife?"
"Miss went to the company. She said you were tired and should rest, so I didn’t wake you."
Tired?
Well, he was a little tired.
"Fine. You can go if there’s nothing else."
Uncle Fu hesitated. "Young Master Lin, should I prepare some tonic soup?"
Lin Ran shot him a look.
"My constitution is fine. Not today."
Lin Ran grumbled inwardly—times had truly changed. Even the butler was looking down on him now. But he was strong, damn it!
Not to boast, but surviving under Luo Yao’s… care was no small feat.
"Understood. I’ll take my leave then."
Lin Ran nodded.
As Uncle Fu walked away, he sighed internally.
"Young Master Lin, always so stubborn about saving face."
After Uncle Fu left, Lin Ran suddenly remembered he hadn’t asked about Granny Wang’s condition.
But before he could dwell on it, something else came to mind.
Lin Ran recalled the note Bi Yaolian had slipped him yesterday and went to retrieve it.
It contained a phone number.
He dialed, and the call was answered almost immediately.
"I knew you’d call."
The voice sounded familiar.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"Luo Wushuang?"
The person on the other end confirmed, "Technically, you should call me ‘Second Uncle.’"
"Don’t push it. You might not be around much longer. What do you want?"
Luo Wushuang was taken aback by Lin Ran’s tone. He double-checked his intel—something didn’t add up.
"I’m proposing a partnership. You want to escape Luo Yao’s control too, don’t you?"
Lin Ran narrowed his eyes. Wasn’t this the same script as Luo Wuyou?
What he didn’t know was that Luo Wushuang was in a league of his own compared to that woman.
Luo Wushuang was cunning, ruthless, and scheming.
The biggest difference? He knew how to bide his time—hence his long disappearance. Luo Wuyou, on the other hand, was impulsive.
Of course, they shared one belief: that Lin Ran was Luo Yao’s plaything, that he despised her and yearned to break free.
"What if I say no?"
Though Lin Ran knew Luo Wushuang wanted an alliance, he played hard to get. Agreeing too quickly would raise suspicion.
Sure enough, Luo Wushuang’s tone remained relaxed.
"Don’t rush to refuse. I know you’re only complying out of fear. But rest assured—I won’t control you. The choice is yours. You could even report this to Luo Yao, but… I doubt you will."
Lin Ran stayed silent, letting the pause linger before replying.
"What’s your goal?"
The voice on the other end was eerily calm. "To reclaim control of the Luo family. Lin Ran, do you know why Luo Yao hasn’t killed me yet? Do you really think it’s because of you?"
Lin Ran scoffed. "What the hell do you know?"
A beat of silence.
"Must we resort to such language?"

chapters.title: Chapter 192
chapters.content:
"Heh, I'm hanging up. Don't bother me again." Lin Ran spoke coldly before ending the call abruptly, leaving Luo Wushuang on the other end stunned.
Ten seconds later, the phone rang again.
"Don’t hang up so fast. There’s something else I need to tell you."
Lin Ran replied impatiently, "Spit it out then."
Suppressing his anger, Luo Wushuang said, "Listen, if you think Luo Yao hasn’t dared to touch me because of you, you’re wrong. I still have value—things she wants are in my hands. And I hold some standing in the Luo family. If she really tries to eliminate me, the rest of the family will turn against her."
"She doesn’t love anyone. To her, you’ll always just be a plaything."
Lin Ran couldn’t help but laugh at the words coming through the phone.
"So? What’s your point?"
"Cooperation."
Lin Ran fell silent for a moment before responding, "I don’t trust you.""You don’t need to trust me. You just need to know what you want."
Feigning a sigh, Lin Ran said, "Fine. I want this kept between just the two of us."
"Of course. I don’t want anyone else knowing either. Lin Ran, once we bring Luo Yao down, I’ll give you more wealth than you could spend in a lifetime—including the place you live now. It’ll all be yours."
Lin Ran curled his lips in disdain.
That’s already mine. Why would I need you to give it to me?
"That doesn’t matter. Just remember your promise. Now, tell me—what’s your plan?"
There was silence on the other end before Luo Wushuang finally spoke. "It’s not safe to discuss over the phone. We should meet in person."
Lin Ran: "Fine. I’ll pick the place."
"That’s not ideal."
"I don’t trust you, so I choose the location."
"Alright. I’ll wait for your message."
After hanging up, Lin Ran narrowed his eyes.
"Things just got interesting."
Meanwhile, Luo Wushuang smirked, as if everything had gone exactly as expected.
"What did Lin Ran say?" Bi Yaolian stood beside him, her remaining hand pressing an electronic voice generator against her throat, producing a hoarse, mechanical sound. Her hatred for Luo Yao had reached its peak.
Luo Yao had stripped her of a woman’s dignity.
"Just as I thought. Lin Ran’s submission to Luo Yao is an act. He agreed to work with me."
Bi Yaolian frowned, recalling Lin Ran’s wild behavior the last time they met at the Luo family estate.
Was all of that just an act? Her distorted voice rasped through the device.
"Could this be a trap?"
"Unlikely. I trust my instincts. My investigation confirmed that Lin Ran’s past has no connection to Luo Yao. Over the years, he’s done everything to escape her control. He’s definitely pretending—he’s just very convincing, which is why you were fooled."
Luo Wushuang narrowed his eyes. "Think about it—how could someone who despises you suddenly fall in love?"
"From the moment Luo Yao met Lin Ran, she showed extreme possessiveness. What man wouldn’t be terrified?"
Bi Yaolian found his reasoning sound.
"So that’s how it is. Husband, once we turn the tables, we must make Luo Yao suffer."
Luo Wushuang’s gaze darkened as he stared at her, making her flinch.
"Husband? What’s wrong?"
"Yesterday, when you passed information to Lin Ran… the bodyguards saw you, didn’t they?"
Bi Yaolian quickly shook her head. "No, no! They didn’t notice."
Luo Wushuang scoffed and said nothing more.
Stupid woman.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Meanwhile, in Luo Corporation’s office, Luo Yao toyed with her phone, her expression unreadable.
"Ah Ran, I’m trusting you so much now. I hope you don’t disappoint me."
Liu Meng knocked and entered.
"President Luo, it’s time to go."
Luo Yao stood and left the office with Liu Meng, departing Luo Corporation.
After a journey of over half an hour, Luo Yao arrived at an underground entertainment den.
When Brother Dao heard of her arrival, tension gripped him.
Outwardly, he was a feared underworld boss, but in truth, he was nothing more than Luo Yao’s loyal subordinate.
The reason? About five years ago, Brother Dao wasn’t yet the undisputed ruler of the underground. Back then, three major factions coexisted, maintaining an uneasy peace—each keeping to their own territory, avoiding conflict, even sharing drinks occasionally.
But peace never lasts. As the saying goes, the empire, long divided, must unite; long united, must divide.
One of the bosses grew ambitious, dreaming of unifying the capital’s underworld—not just for greater profits, but to achieve what no one had in decades.
He invited Brother Dao and the other leader to a meeting, secretly mobilizing all his forces to eliminate them both.
One of them paid with his life.
Brother Dao was stunned. Back then, he still believed in loyalty. Watching one brother betray and kill another, now targeting him, left him broken.
He fled and hid, but the seed of vengeance took root.
Not long after, Brother Dao returned with an unknown force, sweeping through and wiping out the traitor in one swift strike.
When everyone expected him to claim dominance, he shocked them all by declaring that gangs would no longer exist in the capital.
Instead, he opened this underground entertainment den, which slowly became a gold mine.
Though he stepped back from the underworld, new factions still arose. Yet no matter who rose to power, all acknowledged Brother Dao’s status. Everyone still called him Big Brother.
With him around, no upstarts dared challenge the order.
That was Brother Dao’s story.
From a righteous leader to a ruthless yet principled figure, he had transformed.
But few knew his most unexpected identity.
Though his actions seemed reckless, they were actually part of a government strategy.
Criminal elements were like ants—impossible to eradicate completely. With Brother Dao in place, smaller factions stayed in line.
Without him, unruly newcomers would multiply unchecked, eventually forming new powers beyond control.
Using darkness to suppress darkness had always been a tactic.
And sometimes, certain tasks required men like him.
For instance, Brother Dao once helped authorities dismantle a major drug ring, nearly wiping out the capital’s supply—only a trickle remained.
Of course, he owed it all to Luo Yao—not just for helping him take revenge, but for showing him a new path afterward.
Otherwise, he would have long been dead in some back alley.
Brother Dao chose to follow Luo Yao, not just out of fear, but also respect and gratitude.
After all, without Luo Yao's support back then, he would never have gotten his revenge or lived this comfortably now.

chapters.title: Chapter 193
chapters.content:
Luo Yao was willing to help Brother Dao only because she needed someone like him to handle certain tasks for her—a fact Brother Dao had always been well aware of. These tasks included investigating matters that couldn’t be openly discussed or tracking down people who were difficult to find.
Luo Yao gave him a cold glance.
"Where are they?"
Brother Dao pointed toward a highly concealed room. Luo Yao instructed Liu Meng and Brother Dao to stand guard outside while she entered alone.
Inside the dark room, three bodyguards were locked up. The moment Luo Yao stepped in, their eyes widened in terror.
"Betraying me? How bold."
Every bodyguard by Lin Ran’s side had been personally selected and trained by Luo Yao.
But just the day before, she had discovered that Lin Ran’s whereabouts had been leaked. She had captured the culprit, while the other two had been swayed by Little Tong’s influence.
This was also why she had left the manor alone early that morning—she didn’t want Lin Ran to witness the bloody aftermath.
The bodyguard who had exposed Lin Ran’s movements tried to defend himself: "Miss, we didn’t betray you. I only mentioned that Young Master Lin was going to the hospital for a check-up!""Betraying Ah Ran is the same as betraying me."
The bodyguard still clung to a sliver of hope.
"But… I was acting for the Luo family’s sake. Second Master is, after all, your own uncle."
Luo Yao’s eyes gradually darkened, a familiar sensation spreading through her entire body.
"Do you think you’re being funny?"
At the sight of her expression, the three bodyguards broke into a cold sweat. Having served in the manor for years, they knew exactly what that look meant.
Soon, the sealed room echoed with screams.
By the time Luo Yao emerged again, her clothes were drenched in crimson, and the three bodyguards inside had become nothing more than a footnote in history.
"I’ll go clean up. You two handle the mess inside."
After washing off in her private lounge, Liu Meng brought her a fresh set of clothes.
When Luo Yao reappeared in the entertainment district, Brother Dao had already tidied up the remnants.
"Boss, what should we do about those enemies of Young Master Lin?"
A playful tone laced his words.
"If Ah Ran wants to play, let him. The moment he’s done, hand them over to me."
"Understood, Boss."
Only after Luo Yao left did Brother Dao finally exhale in relief.
He hadn’t interacted with her often, but every encounter left him feeling the weight of death looming over him.
He muttered to himself, "She’s the one person in the entire Blue Star no one dares to cross."
When Luo Yao returned to Luo Corporation, she was met with a sight that ignited her killing intent.
"Take her out."
"Right away, President Luo." Liu Meng complied, recognizing the murderous glint in Luo Yao’s eyes.
Half an hour earlier, Lin Ran had hung up Luo Wushuang’s call, pocketed his phone, and headed out with his bodyguards.
Naturally, he was looking for Luo Yao.
They had been apart for hours, and if he didn’t see her soon, Lin Ran felt like he would die.
Besides, they had an agreement—if they weren’t at the manor, they had to stay together.
Though it sometimes felt like being caged, Lin Ran never resisted. He couldn’t bear the thought of making Luo Yao even slightly unhappy.
Soon, Lin Ran pulled up in front of Luo Corporation’s building. But when he glanced up, he was met with an unexpected sight—Huo Haini, whom he hadn’t seen in ages, was standing there as if waiting for him.
"Lin Ran, where’s Miss Luo?"
Huo Haini had been wanting to approach Lin Ran for a while, but every time, he was with Luo Yao, making her too afraid to get close.
Today, by sheer coincidence, she had finally caught him alone.
"What’s it to you?"
"Lin Ran, what a coincidence! Let’s chat, shall we?"
Lin Ran couldn’t fathom Huo Haini’s thought process. Had she already forgotten how he’d kicked her out of his car last time?
"What now? Another one of your outrageous declarations?"
Huo Haini gazed at Lin Ran, mesmerized by how manly, handsome, and wealthy he was.
He was exactly the kind of boyfriend she had always dreamed of.
"Lin Ran, I like you. I’ve liked you for so long. Back when you were chasing Liu Ruxue, I was jealous of her, so I acted like I hated you. But now that you don’t like her anymore, why not make me your girlfriend?"
Huo Haini felt her previous confession hadn’t been convincing enough, so today, with Luo Yao absent, she decided to try again.
After all, Lin Ran was the wealthiest man she could ever hope to get close to—Chairman of Suran Group, owner of Nuanyao Group.
"What nonsense are you spouting? Don’t you know I’m married?"
Huo Haini was well aware of Lin Ran’s situation. She had been at the school event too, and she thought his grand gesture was incredibly romantic.
But why did Luo Yao have to be the one on that stage instead of her?
"Lin Ran, you could divorce Luo Yao and be with me instead. I wouldn’t hold it against you. Once we’re married, you can focus on your career while I manage the household and your assets. I could even bear your children. Doesn’t that sound perfect?"
Huo Haini was convinced Lin Ran no longer loved Liu Ruxue, but she refused to believe he loved Luo Yao either.
That woman was downright unhinged. Any sane man would steer clear of her—who could possibly love someone like that?
Lin Ran must have only acted that way out of fear.
What she didn’t know was that Lin Ran was anything but normal.
"Huo Haini, you and Liu Ruxue really are cut from the same cloth—both love playing the other woman. Too bad I’ve got no taste for green tea. Why don’t you go find some stray dogs on the street? After all, humans don’t eat garbage."
As he spoke, Lin Ran pondered how best to teach Huo Haini a lesson.
Sometimes, she was even more insufferable than Liu Ruxue.
Huo Haini: "Lin Ran, even if you insult me, I don’t care. Admit it—you don’t love Luo Yao. As for Liu Ruxue, she only ever saw you as a backup plan, a pathetic simp. But with me, you’d always be my number one. I’d never take advantage of you like they did. I’d only ever cherish you."
Lin Ran was utterly dumbfounded. What kind of delusional fairy-tale logic was this?
Where did she get such confidence? Did someone hand it to her?
Just then, Liu Ruxue’s voice rang out from behind Huo Haini.
"Nini, I never thought you’d stoop this low."
Lin Ran froze for a second before signaling his bodyguards to bring him a chair.
This was going to be good.
Huo Haini stiffened but quickly regained her composure.
Turning around, she retorted, "What about me? What kind of person am I?"
Liu Ruxue stared at her in disbelief.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Life at school had become unbearable for her—everywhere she went, people pointed fingers, and some even lashed out physically.
Her family had vanished without a trace, ignoring all her calls.
With nowhere else to go, she had rented a place off-campus. Today, she had come hoping to catch Lin Ran by chance, to ask if he had been the one behind those videos at the school event—and why he had done it.
But instead, she had walked into this scene.

chapters.title: Chapter 194
chapters.content:
"Nini, I heard everything. You just confessed to Lin Ran. I never thought you'd be this kind of person."
Huo Haini.
"Liu Ruxue, don’t make it sound so ugly. I’ve always tolerated you, given in to you, and even helped you scheme—all because I genuinely considered you a sister. But you lost Lin Ran because of your own stupidity."
"Nini, you—"
"What? You won’t even let me speak now? Who else can you blame for your own foolishness? You’re such a two-faced flirt, always stringing guys along, and now you expect me to help you win Lin Ran back?"
Liu Ruxue’s chest heaved with anger.
"Why? Why are you doing this to me? I treated you like a sister, and yet you like Lin Ran?"
Huo Haini scoffed. "So what if I like Lin Ran? Does he have your name written on him? Why can’t I compete for him?"
"Do you really think everything you want automatically belongs to you, Liu Ruxue? You self-righteous bitch."
At that moment, Huo Haini snapped.She couldn’t keep pretending anymore. Every time she was with Liu Ruxue, all the guys would orbit around her.
It had been eating at her for a long time.
She’d held it in again and again, but now she couldn’t take it anymore. She might as well lay it all out today. That way, the next time she saw Lin Ran, she could compete openly.
But what she didn’t realize was that she was about to face the harsest punishment of her life.
Liu Ruxue was stunned. This was the first time Huo Haini had ever spoken to her like this.
She had always considered Huo Haini her closest friend, someone she trusted with everything—including her feelings for Lin Ran. Because she once believed that sisterhood far outweighed any man.
Men could be replaced, but true friends were rare.
But now—
Liu Ruxue screamed, "Huo Haini, what have I ever done to wrong you? Why would you betray me and steal my man behind my back?"The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Huo Haini laughed coldly.
"Ha! You’re hilarious. ‘Your man’? Liu Ruxue, get a grip. Lin Ran was never yours. In the past, he was your simp. Now, you’re his."
"You—!" Liu Ruxue felt like her lungs were about to explode from rage.
Huo Haini: "From today on, we’re done."
With that, Huo Haini shot Lin Ran a coy smile and walked away without another glance. She didn’t want to stay and watch Liu Ruxue’s pitiful act—as if she were the victim here.
Liu Ruxue collapsed to the ground, sobbing.
Seeing that the catfight was over and there was nothing left to spectate, Lin Ran turned to leave.
Liu Ruxue suddenly cried out, "Lin Ran, I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! I was wrong—this time, I truly know I was wrong!"
But Lin Ran ignored her. Liu Ruxue couldn’t even push past his bodyguards.
Desperate, she pulled out her phone and tapped on Lin Ran’s profile.
[I’m sorry. I always thought Huo Haini was my best friend. I never imagined she’d betray me like this. I regret everything—I shouldn’t have listened to her. Lin Ran, please stay with me. I’m in so much pain.]
She hit send.
A red exclamation mark appeared.
Liu Ruxue broke down completely.
In that moment, she suddenly remembered all the times Lin Ran had been good to her.
Every time she needed help, he was there, standing in front of her like a hero. But what had she done in return?
She took it all for granted.
Back then, she really had been the most important person in Lin Ran’s life.
She was so sure of it—even his own family couldn’t compare.
That’s why she refused to believe he didn’t love her anymore.
But his indifference now crushed her.
"I really lost him… wu wu wu!"
After crying for a while, Liu Ruxue suddenly felt an urge to return to their old campus.
So she disguised herself and went back.
Luckily, the chilly weather made masks and hats normal, so no one recognized her. Otherwise, she’d have been swarmed again.
Walking across the school grounds, memories flooded back.
That time Lin Ran confessed to her right here on this field.
And the basketball court where he used to play.
Outside the dormitory, where he once told her, "I’ll make you the happiest woman in the world."
Her response back then? "I don’t want to date before graduation, Lin Ran. Don’t pressure me."
Remembering the warmth in his eyes that day, Liu Ruxue smiled.
But staring at the empty dormitory now, her smile twisted into tears.
They fell like broken strings of pearls.
The man who loved her most was gone. Her best friend had betrayed her.
Lin Ran used to be so pure, so devoted to her—and she had thrown him away?
This time, she truly understood her mistake.
"Wu wu wu! Lin Ran, I know I was wrong! Please forgive me! Why won’t you look back at me? Didn’t you love me the most?"
Just as Liu Ruxue was drowning in despair, a girl approached her.
"Liu Ruxue!"
"No, I’m not—" Liu Ruxue quickly denied.
The girl sighed.
"I get it. I know how you feel about Lin Ran."
Liu Ruxue stared at her in shock—had she finally found someone who understood?
"Who are you?"
"Just a junior. I’ve liked someone for a long time too, so I know what you’re going through."
Liu Ruxue frowned, confused. Why was this stranger telling her this?
"I had a crush on a senior, but my best friend kept manipulating me into testing him. But I was luckier than you—now, we’re together."
Liu Ruxue’s eyes lit up.
"Really? Then can I—? Why won’t Lin Ran forgive me? I was just manipulated by Huo Haini too! And that thing with Lin Jian—he tricked me! I was just a victim! I’ve always loved Lin Ran the most. Why doesn’t he get that?"
The girl’s eyes filled with pity, but inside, she was screaming.
Oh my god, what kind of delusional princess is this?
"Do you know why Lin Ran won’t take you back?"
"Why?"
"Because of Huo Haini. He resents her. Every time he sees you, he remembers how you neglected him—and Huo Haini was the one who orchestrated it all."
Liu Ruxue’s gaze sharpened.
"I bet Huo Haini repeatedly told you not to commit to Lin Ran but also not to let him go, right? It was that push-and-pull that made him give up on you completely."
She was right. This was all Huo Haini’s fault.
Liu Ruxue remembered clearly—there was a time she had been so moved by Lin Ran, ready to say yes, but Huo Haini intervened, convincing her to "test him for a few more years."

chapters.title: Chapter 195
chapters.content:
"Why are you telling me all this?"
"Because I genuinely feel for you. Seeing you now is like looking at my past self. Do you know how happy I am? My senior just proposed to me yesterday."
Liu Ruxue's sorrow melted into excitement, her face lighting up with a smile.
She could almost picture it—Lin Ran divorcing Luo Yao and then proposing to her instead.
"How exactly did you manage it?"
The girl's lips curled into a smirk as she locked eyes with Liu Ruxue. "Because I proved my determination to the person I love."
Liu Ruxue grew even more puzzled.
"Proved your determination? How?"
"I turned my former best friend into an enemy, ensuring she’d never interfere with our relationship again."
Liu Ruxue’s expression turned blank."Never interfere…?"
"Right. But that was my method—it might not work for you. What you do is up to you. Just remember, you have to be ruthless. Otherwise, your enemy will retaliate like crazy once they recover."
Liu Ruxue: "Did your friend ever retaliate?"
The girl’s gaze hardened. "My friend? She never got the chance."
With that, the girl walked away, leaving Liu Ruxue standing there, stunned.
What did that mean?
How could she ensure her enemy never got the opportunity for revenge?
Liu Ruxue’s rationality began slipping away.
Yes… it was time to end this fake friendship with Huo Haini once and for all.
---
Luo Corporation.
As Lin Ran approached, he noticed everyone in the company staring at him strangely.
Did he have something on his face?
These people were acting weird.
What he didn’t know was that every employee at Luo Corporation was screaming internally: "Ah—!"
Why was this guy back? Here to flaunt his relationship again?
Inner monologue: [Groundhog screech], insert meme face here. (?0?)
When Lin Ran reached Luo Yao’s office, she wasn’t there.
Neither was Liu Meng.
Assuming they were in a meeting or handling business, he pushed open the office door.
"What do you think you’re doing?" A vaguely familiar voice called out. Lin Ran turned.
Well, well. The little troublemaker.
"You’re that… what’s-your-name? Schemer?"
"Zhang Xinyan."
"Oh, right. What do you want?"
"Who gave you permission to enter? Company rules state no one enters the CEO’s office without approval from President Luo or Assistant Liu."
Lin Ran: "I’d advise you to stop talking to me."
"What’s that supposed to mean?"
"Exactly what it sounds like. Once, a woman talked to me. Your President Luo slapped her unconscious."
Zhang Xinyan frowned.
"That’s impossible. You’re lying. Hitting people is illegal."
Lin Ran’s eyebrow twitched. "Excuse me? Are you saying my wife doesn’t have the right to slap you?"
Zhang Xinyan paused, realizing Lin Ran had a point—Luo Yao absolutely had that authority.
She wavered, unsure whether to let him in.
Letting him in broke the rules, but stopping him might get her punished.
Being an employee was tough.
Just then, another assistant pulled her aside.
"Are you insane? That’s Young Master Lin—President Luo’s most treasured man. The last person you want to mess with."
Zhang Xinyan rolled her eyes, muttering defiantly.
"What’s so great about a freeloader anyway?"
The senior assistant, Wang Jie, froze, giving her a strange look.
"Zhang Xinyan, grow a brain. Do you have a death wish, spouting nonsense like that?"
Zhang Xinyan stuck out her tongue but remained stubborn.
Even Lin Ran’s friend—what was his name? Wu Zhishang—was just as annoying.
Little did she know, Wu Zhishang would soon teach her a harsh lesson.
---
Lin Ran waited in the office briefly before Luo Yao returned.
Instead of looking pleased to see him, she asked suspiciously:Thɪs
"While I was gone… you didn’t talk to any other women, did you?"
Lin Ran nearly choked. Did Luo Yao plant a bug on him? How did she always know?
"I did, but it wasn’t my fault. Zhang Xinyan stopped me from entering."
Luo Yao: "You talked to Zhang Xinyan?"
Again?
Lin Ran admitted freely.
"Not just Zhang Xinyan. I also ran into Liu Ruxue—but I didn’t say a single word to her."
Luo Yao’s smile turned chilling. "Did Liu Ruxue’s pitiful act stir up your protective instincts?"
Lin Ran immediately raised his hands. "Wife, I swear on our son Lin Tianba’s life—if I spoke to her, may he become a worthless turtle."
Luo Yao gave him a strange look but nodded. "Fine, I’ll believe you for now. But I heard Huo Haini confessed to you?"
Oddly, Lin Ran wasn’t nervous about this one.
What kind of idiot would fall for Huo Haini?
"She did. But I ignored her. The sight of her disgusts me. Wife, you’re not seriously jealous of her, are you? She’s not even fit to shine your shoes. Just have her eliminated."
Luo Yao fell silent for a moment.
"Huo Haini… won’t live much longer."
Lin Ran: ???
"Wait, you’re actually jealous?"
Instead of answering, Luo Yao called Liu Meng in.
"Liu Meng, how long have you worked for me?"
Liu Meng broke into a cold sweat.
"E-eight years."
"Hmm. That long, yet you can’t even manage your subordinates?"
Liu Meng was baffled.
"That Zhang Xinyan—she’s fired. Effective tomorrow. One more slip-up, and you’re out too."
Liu Meng instantly understood—Zhang Xinyan must’ve provoked Lin Ran again.
Without hesitation, she had Zhang Xinyan pack her things and leave.
When Zhang Xinyan got the news, she was stunned.
"Why?"
"No reason. You’re just not a good fit for Luo Corporation."
Obviously, it’s because you offended someone you shouldn’t have. Why even ask?
Liu Meng thought to herself: Be grateful you only annoyed Young Master Lin instead of falling for him. Otherwise, you wouldn’t leave here alive.
Zhang Xinyan felt like the sky had fallen. With no choice, she left Luo Corporation.
The autumn air was cold, but not as cold as her heart.
Tears streamed down her face as she walked through the biting wind.
She had beaten countless competitors to join Luo Corporation’s assistant team—only to be dismissed just like that.
Sure, the company would pay a penalty, but money meant nothing to her.
What mattered was being able to prove her worth.
Once Liu Meng reported Zhang Xinyan’s termination, Luo Yao’s expression softened, and Lin Ran finally relaxed.
Looks like he dodged a beating this time.
Close call.
Luo Yao continued, "A’Ran, about Liu Ruxue, Huo Haini, Zhang Xinyan, Zhang Xiaonuan…"

chapters.title: Chapter 196
chapters.content:
Lin Ran immediately cut her off, saying, "Darling, I love you. I don’t want anyone but you—I won’t even glance at anyone else. Right now, all I want is you..."
After wrapping up a business deal worth hundreds of millions, Liu Meng knocked on the door.
"President Luo, Young Master Lin, a popular show has extended an invitation. They’d like to know if you’d be interested in participating."
Luo Yao and Lin Ran exchanged puzzled looks.
Had Liu Meng lost her mind?
With their status, why would they ever need to appear on an interview show?
In fact, even Liu Meng had been stunned when she first heard the request. But the assistant’s explanation had instantly enlightened her.
Seeing the skeptical expressions on Lin Ran and Luo Yao’s faces, Liu Meng didn’t dare delay and quickly clarified.
"This interview program is quite famous—it’s called The Boss and His Better Half. It primarily features successful entrepreneurs, though they occasionally invite celebrities as well. The show documents their weekend routines, but since it’s a live broadcast, it would require some of your time on Sunday morning. President Luo, what do you think?"
After delivering her pitch, Liu Meng waited for Luo Yao’s response.There were two reasons she had brought this to Luo Yao.
First, as the president’s executive assistant, she knew her boss well—anything involving Young Master Lin was something Luo Yao would be interested in.
The second reason was far more mischievous. The assistant had remarked, "We get fed dog food every day, while others miss out. Isn’t that just unfair?"
And so, this devious reasoning became Liu Meng’s motivation.
Why should we be the only ones suffering?
Let the whole world experience this "joy" too.
Let everyone see just how shamelessly lovey-dovey their boss and her husband could be.
Of course, Liu Meng had one concern—whether Lin Ran would agree to participate. After all, the final decision rested with him.
Luo Yao turned to Lin Ran and asked, "A-Ran, do you want to do this?"
Without a second thought, Lin Ran replied, "I’ll go along with whatever you decide."
Luo Yao lowered her head in thought.
As the young lady of the foremost financial conglomerate, appearing on such a program would be beneath her dignity.
But the thought of flaunting her relationship with Lin Ran in front of the entire internet, declaring to the world "This man is mine," sent her spiraling into a honey-sweet euphoria.
It would also serve as a warning to any woman who dared set her sights on Lin Ran.
A feeling called "desire" exploded in Luo Yao’s heart.
"Fine, go ahead and schedule it."
Seeing Luo Yao’s agreement, Liu Meng added, "Oh, President Luo, the show might also ask some rather personal questions. That’s actually why it’s so popular."
"Got it."
With Luo Yao raising no objections, Liu Meng was practically giddy with delight.
Everyone thinks my job as the executive assistant is so easy, huh? Just wait—in a couple of days, they’ll see just how "easy" it really is.
With that, Liu Meng promptly contacted the production team.
The show’s director was in the studio, preparing materials for other guests when the assistant director approached him.
"Director, didn’t we already invite Luo Yao and Lin Ran? Why are you still prepping questions for other people?"
The director looked at him as if he were an idiot. "What kind of nobodies are we? Do you really think Luo Yao would ever agree to appear on our show?"
The assistant director frowned. "Then why did you have me send the invitation?"
"It was just a symbolic gesture to appease the audience. Lin Ran’s popularity is through the roof right now—everyone wants to see him. But who is President Luo? Forget her, even Lin Ran is way out of our league. Our backers can’t even compare to them. We’re not in the same stratosphere, got it?"
Seeing the assistant director’s confusion, the director sighed and continued impatiently.
"Let’s be real—our boss is just a seasoned entrepreneur in the entertainment industry. The guests we usually get are either B-list celebrities or small-time business owners with a bit of clout. Do you really think a financial giant like the Luo Corporation would give us the time of day?"
Can’t find the book by title? Try searching the author—maybe they just changed their name!
"To put it bluntly, our boss is worth a few billion at most. He only got this show off the ground because of his seniority in the industry. In front of real financial dynasties, we’re nothing."
The assistant director hesitated. "But what if...?"
"There is no ‘what if.’ That scenario doesn’t exist. If it somehow happens, I’ll stand on my head and... well, you get the idea."
The assistant director sighed at the director’s brutal self-awareness.
Just then, his phone rang.
Seeing an impeccably prestigious number flash on the screen, he scrambled to answer.
"Hello?"
"Hello, this is Liu Meng, assistant to President Luo of the Luo Corporation. Regarding your show’s invitation, President Luo and her husband, Lin Ran, have agreed to participate. You may proceed with filming the day after tomorrow."
"W-what?" The assistant director stood frozen like a wooden chicken.
Liu Meng continued, "I said President Luo has agreed to appear on an episode of your show. Make the necessary preparations, and coordinate the rest with me directly."
After hanging up, the assistant director remained motionless, phone still pressed to his ear.Thɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
The director snapped, "What’s wrong with you? If you’ve got nothing to do, go work. Why are you staring at me like that?"
"Director."
"Yeah?"
"What exactly does ‘standing on your head and...’ look like?"
Director: "???"
At Skyreach Manor, Uncle Fu left the main villa and knocked on the door of the servants’ quarters.
Soon, a familiar voice called out from inside.
"Who is it?"
"It’s me."
After a long pause, the door opened. Granny Wang looked at Uncle Fu and asked, "What do you need?"
Uncle Fu handed her a card.
"This is compensation from Young Master Lin and the young lady. Take it."
Granny Wang didn’t refuse—she needed the money.
"If that’s all, Uncle Fu, you may leave now."
Uncle Fu frowned. "Don’t you have anything else to say to me?"
"What should I say? That I left without a word back then? Or why I disappeared so suddenly?"
"Isn’t that the truth?"
"Yes, and I’m not denying it. What else do you want? To use your authority as the butler to fire me?" For once, a trace of anger flickered across Granny Wang’s face.
Uncle Fu sighed and turned to leave, bewildered by what he had done wrong.
Watching Uncle Fu’s retreating figure, Granny Wang’s eyes dimmed, returning to their usual dullness. She sighed inwardly.
Some things, once missed, are gone forever. The present is all that matters.
But why couldn’t she hide the loneliness in her eyes?
Before long, Lin Ran and Luo Yao returned. Since the next day was the weekend, they were both in good spirits.
"Uncle Fu, what’s going on with you lately? You seem completely drained."
Uncle Fu forced a smile. "Do I? Young Master Lin, you must be mistaken."
"Am I?"
Seeing Uncle Fu’s denial, Lin Ran didn’t press further.
The truth will come out eventually. You can’t hide it forever.
"The day after tomorrow, a film crew will be coming to the manor for recording. Make the necessary arrangements."

chapters.title: Chapter 197
chapters.content:
Uncle Fu was taken aback. "The program crew? Are they here to film a short drama?"
"No, they're here to document my daily life with Luo Yao. It's a very popular show."
Uncle Fu's mind was in turmoil. He couldn't quite comprehend such a thing, but his professionalism quickly helped him regain his composure.
"Understood, Young Master Lin."
On Saturday, Lin Ran had no plans to go out.
First, because these were extraordinary times. Though he had agreed to cooperate with Luo Wushuang, he couldn't be sure whether this was just a ploy to lower his guard before using him to threaten Luo Yao.
Second, because he was lazy and didn’t feel like leaving.
"Darling, how about we spend the day exploring the estate? I haven’t really taken the time to properly tour it yet."
Luo Yao replied, "Sure!" Wherever Lin Ran wanted to go, she would follow—even to the ends of the earth.
The estate was enormous, and Lin Ran had only visited a handful of places.How big was it? In his past life, he had tried to escape once—just once—before giving up.
Aside from the main gate, there was no way out. It was easy to get lost.
Today, on a whim, he wanted to explore the entire estate—partly out of laziness, partly out of curiosity.
Aside from that one time he got lost, Lin Ran had only been to Villa No. 1, the sky garden, the secret chamber, and the crocodile pond. These places were just the tip of the iceberg.
The two arrived at the private zoo, where the exotic animals were unmatched by anything outside.
Though Lin Ran had always known about the private zoo on the estate, this was his first visit—even in his past life, he had never been.
The only animals he had seen before were the crocodiles in the pond and two snow leopards.
He had fed the crocodiles pesticide, and the snow leopards… well, they got a different kind of treatment—aphrodisiacs.
As the saying goes: One mounts, one moans, next year the cubs will greet you with grins.
Remembering the past, Lin Ran couldn’t help but chuckle.
"What’s so funny, A-Ran?"
Lin Ran pointed at the two peacocks in the glass enclosure. "I was just thinking—what if we separated them? Wouldn’t that be amusing?"
"Uncle Fu, separate them."
Lin Ran quickly stopped him. "Hey, hey, hey! No need! I was just joking. They’re a pair—why split them up? It’d be like someone trying to separate you and me..."
"No such person exists, A-Ran. No one will ever be able to tear us apart. If anyone dares try, I guarantee they won’t live to see the next sunrise."
Lin Ran: "Exactly. So, can we spare these two creatures? If you separate them, you might as well turn them into dinner."
"Did you hear that? A-Ran wants to eat them. Take them out."
Uncle Fu wiped his sweat, but Lin Ran stopped him again.
"Darling, I don’t actually want to eat them. I only want to eat you."
Luo Yao’s eyes softened with affection. "If anything, I should be eating you."
The zoo emptied—bodyguards, butlers, and servants all retreated. Every animal averted its gaze.
After a battle for the ages, Luo Yao asked:
"A-Ran, is there anything you’re keeping from me?"
Lin Ran feigned confusion. "I don’t think so? I’ve already confessed everything."
A flicker of something unreadable passed through Luo Yao’s eyes.
"Oh! Right! I almost forgot—Luo Wushuang reached out to me. If you hadn’t asked, I might’ve completely blanked on it."
Luo Yao’s heart eased, but her gaze turned icy.
"I’m glad you told me, A-Ran. But the fact that I had to pry it out of you… I don’t like that."
Lin Ran: "I’m sorry, darling. I really just forgot. Honestly, it’s not even important to me."
"Then what is important?"
"You, of course. You’re the only thing I care about. The only reason I’m alive in this world is to love you properly."
Luo Yao’s heart swelled with emotion. Her feelings were becoming more complex by the day.
Gazing into Lin Ran’s eyes, she asked, "What does Luo Wushuang want from you?"
(Note: This site uses cookie technology to save your "reading history" and "bookshelf," so clearing browser cookies or reinstalling the browser may cause your progress to disappear. We recommend occasionally taking screenshots of your bookshelf to avoid losing track of your current novel!)
Truthfully, Luo Yao already knew. She just wanted to hear the answer from Lin Ran’s lips.
"Obviously, he thinks I’m useful. But since we haven’t met yet, I don’t know the specifics."
Lin Ran paused, then added, "But I can guess. He probably wants to use me against you—or maybe capture me to threaten you."
"And what do you want to do about it, A-Ran?"
Lin Ran looked at her in disbelief. The old Luo Yao would never have asked such a question.
She would’ve acted on her own instincts.
Even last time, when she agreed not to lock him in the secret chamber, it was only after his… persistent efforts.
But now, she was actually asking for his opinion.
"I was thinking… we could play along."
"But I don’t want you taking risks."
Lin Ran: "Darling, life is full of risks. You could get hit by a flowerpot just walking downstairs. Besides, I know you’ll protect me."
Uncle Fu, listening nearby, found this exchange odd.
Who talks like that?
Shouldn’t it be, "I believe I can handle it?"
How could Young Master Lin so casually defer to the young mistress’s protection? Are you even a man?
After spending so much time around the couple, Uncle Fu was starting to feel a little sour.
Luo Yao, however, pulled Lin Ran close and murmured, "Of course. I’ll always protect you, A-Ran."
Lin Ran had expected to spend hours convincing her. He never imagined she’d agree so easily.
It seemed that in this world, not only had he changed—Luo Yao was changing too.
"Darling, no matter what happens, I want to face it together with you."
"Okay."
Lin Ran’s heart soared.
"Uncle Fu."
"Young Master Lin."
"Clear the area. Prepare the bath."
"Right away."
This time, even the animals were locked away.
The entire zoo was silent—save for the sounds of two people.
Lin Ran wanted Luo Yao to understand: his love for her wasn’t confined to home or the office. It could flourish anywhere.
After their "day of exploration," the program recording awaited them the next day.
Early Sunday morning, the crew arrived at the estate to set up equipment.
The sheer opulence of the place left them dazzled.
That Luo Yao had agreed to the interview was a genuine shock to the program team.
This show had a unique feature: its Q&A segment could get explosive—sometimes downright racy.
Since questions were pulled from live audience comments, anything could happen. And the host? She was relentless, digging deep into the private lives of the elite.
Logically, such a brazen show shouldn’t exist. But its backer was a powerful capitalist who knew exactly what the masses craved: juicy details about the rich and famous.
Many guests gritted their teeth through the humiliation—what could they do? The show’s owner outranked them.
As for the celebrities? They sought out the exposure.
So Luo Yao’s acceptance? That sent shockwaves through the entire production.
After all, it was the first time recording a show with the daughter of a financial tycoon, so the production team had to be extra cautious. They held an emergency meeting overnight to discuss the details.

chapters.title: Chapter 198
chapters.content:
In the end, it was decided to cancel the segment where they respond to live comments.
This show has had its share of mishaps before—like the last episode with the female boss, who was drenched in sweat under the program's questioning, giving answers that made no sense at all, while her husband outright lost his temper on the spot.
Then, one live comment exposed the fact that the boss was keeping a young lover.
The two ended up in a domestic violence scene, forcing the show to be interrupted.
But those were just ordinary business owners—no big deal. Today, however, they were interviewing Luo Yao and Lin Ran, and they couldn’t afford to mess this up.
At 8 a.m., the live broadcast began.
The moment it started, hundreds of thousands of viewers flooded in, with the numbers rising at an astonishing rate.
Host: "Hello, everyone! I’m your old friend Liu Yishou. Today, we’re honored to be at the private estate of the CEO of Luo Corporation—this is also where Luo Yao and Lin Ran live."
Immediately, Luo Yao and Lin Ran’s profiles appeared on the live broadcast screen.
Live comments:[What’s Even Real]: Holy crap! The show actually got Luo Yao and Lin Ran? For real? I thought they were joking!
[Harry Potter Fan]: This place is ridiculously luxurious. That vase by the entrance could probably buy my entire life.
Before the university anniversary celebration, very few people had seen Luo Yao’s real face. The classmates who saw her at the freshman party had their photos deleted on the spot by bodyguards.
But the last university anniversary was live-streamed nationwide, and everyone finally got a glimpse of her. Photos of her started spreading like wildfire online.
Though the footage wasn’t crystal clear—just a few seconds of video and some blurry photos—it was enough to leave countless people in awe.
Host: "Honestly, when I first arrived here, I was stunned by the sheer opulence. We’ve interviewed many celebrities and business owners before, but compared to this, those places seem almost insignificant."
"We’ll be recording here for the entire morning, and I’m sure you’re all as excited as I am. Now, let’s follow the camera into the owners’ home."
As the camera moved, the grand hall of the villa came into view. Uncle Fu gestured for them to enter.
Just that simple gesture instantly ignited the live chat.
[Not the Emperor’s Uncle]: Is this the butler of a luxury estate? This uncle is way too handsome!
[Arrogant Ultraman]: Even the maids in the background are stunning. The life of the rich is truly unpretentious.
As the crew settled in, Lin Ran walked down first and took a seat on the central sofa in the hall.
The cameraman immediately focused on him, and Lin Ran waved at the camera.
"Hey, everyone."
One of the reasons this show is so popular is that it’s completely unscripted and live—no one knows what’ll happen next.
Host: "Good morning, Mr. Lin. Where’s President Luo?"
Lin Ran glanced back toward the staircase—sure enough, Luo Yao appeared there with her usual icy expression. Once she reached the first floor and sat down, her cold gaze swept over the camera.
The two of them delivered a visual feast to the entire internet.
[Voice Ruined from Singing]: AHHHHH! Lin Ran is so handsome, and Luo Yao is so beautiful! What level of loser am I to witness such perfection?
[Attack of the Green Giant]: The show is insane! I thought the promo about filming the top tycoons today was fake—but it’s actually real?
[Love Guru]: Wow, is this the heiress of the top financial empire? She’s unreal—what kind of divine beauty is this?
[Crayon Grudge]: That aura is unmatched. No socialite can compare. Seriously, Lin Ran gets to eat this well every day? I’m jealous.
The host smiled. "President Luo, Mr. Lin, hello."
Lin Ran returned the smile. "Just call us by our names. I don’t like being called ‘President’—it makes me think of ‘edema’ or ‘cyst’ or something."
Lin Ran’s joke broke the ice, and the host relaxed a little.
"Got it. I didn’t expect you to be so humorous. Since you’re familiar with our show, did you prepare anything in advance?"
Luo Yao’s cold eyes flicked toward Liu Yishou. "I’m not familiar with it, and I don’t need to prepare."
Host: "..."
[Tang Bohu Lights Mosquito Coils]: Luo Yao’s stare is the coldest I’ve ever seen. I swear, if she looked at me like that, I’d drop to the floor and play dead.
[Stirring the Pot]: You’d end up actually dead. Don’t you know? Luo Yao despises men.
[Alpaca is an Animal]: Then how did Lin Ran win her over?
[+V for Secret Crab Roe Recipe]: Lin Ran’s looks are explosive too. They’re literally the perfect match.
[Mage Casting Spells]: Now this is what I call a true ice queen.
Liu Yishou swallowed hard. Luo Yao’s presence was overwhelming—stronger than anyone she’d ever interviewed.
It was kind of terrifying.
Lin Ran gently placed his hand over Luo Yao’s, calming her restless mood.
Even though Luo Yao had agreed to this recording, being surrounded by so many staff clearly made her uncomfortable.
Her cold demeanor was just a habit—her real thoughts might very well involve stabbing everyone here.
Lin Ran turned to the host. "Shall we begin?"
"Of course. Following the show’s format, the first segment is a quick Q&A."
The host glanced at the two of them. Seeing no objections, she continued.
"The first question is for Mr. Lin Ran. How do you feel about today’s recording?"
Lin Ran frowned. "Really? That’s the kind of shallow question you’re going with? Why not ask me what my dreams are?"
The host stiffened. She didn’t want to either, but it was the higher-ups’ decision.
Live comments exploded:
[My Readers Get Rich]: Exactly! Why aren’t they picking questions from the live chat today?
[Fifty Sky Gang]: Do you know who these two are? No one dares to let the chat decide.
[Oh My Borscht]: The show always claims to ‘keep it real’—what a joke.
The host awkwardly looked at the director.
The director frowned, but Lin Ran seemed to read their hesitation.
"Just do it like you normally would. No need for special treatment—it’s not like we’re bullying your show."
The director almost wanted to give Lin Ran a thumbs-up. He nodded at the host.
Host: "Alright, let’s move on to today’s first segment—Morning Q&A."
"Crew, get ready. 3, 2, 1—freeze the chat for a question!"
The live comments on the big screen stopped, and the first question appeared:The source of this content ɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
