Meanwhile, Shanghai was anything but peaceful.
The Lu Family and Wang Family were drowning in chaos—especially the Lu Family.
Wang Dacong of the Wang Family only had personal scandals to worry about. As the eldest son, he could throw money at most problems, and Wang Xiaolin was actively cleaning up his messes without shielding him.
The women collectively suing Wang Dacong were either negotiated with or compensated. Even the computer repairman who leaked the scandal was let off the hook.
This magnanimity somewhat improved the Wang Family’s public image.
But what really surprised people was Wang Xiaolin’s stance on his son:
"Handle him as the law demands. Execute him if necessary."
The crisis didn’t harm the Wang Family’s conglomerate—it even salvaged some reputation.
But the goodwill was short-lived. As Wang Dacong’s scandals simmered, old accusations of box office fraud resurfaced.
Wang Family’s cinemas across the country stood empty, much to the delight of rival theater owners. Even their real estate projects stalled.
Wang Xiaolin was exhausted—his hair seemed grayer overnight.
The Lu Family’s troubles were worse.
Customs at the Wang Family’s port had seized 500 kilograms of drugs.
Enough to warrant executions for many.
Previously, the Lu Family had flown under the radar—partly because they’d been careful, partly because their influence deterred scrutiny in a city like Shanghai.
Who’d expect a family of their stature to traffic drugs?
But this time was different. The tipster had revealed the Lu Family’s smuggling method, forcing authorities to act.
Sure enough, the drugs were found at the port.
Their method was ingenious: dissolved in water, absorbed into towels, then shipped overseas for extraction and purification.

chapters.title: Chapter 339
chapters.content:
The fact that such a covert method was uncovered by the informant proves one thing—the evidence must be irrefutable.
No one would dare ignore this kind of report.
If not for the Lu Family's extensive connections, they would have already been taken in for investigation.
But now, things aren’t much better—it’s only a matter of time.
At this moment, a half-dead man hung in the Lu Family ancestral hall. All the core members of the family were present, including Lu Youqi.
"You disgraceful son! I’ve told you before—the Lu Family can do anything, except touch this stuff. Did you think my words were just for show?"
Having been hung from daybreak until late at night, Lu Ludu could no longer speak. Merely clinging to life was a miracle.
"If you wanted to ruin yourself, fine, but you had to drag the entire Lu Family down with you. If you were so bold, why didn’t you tell me earlier? I could’ve sent you to a war-torn country to face reality. Who knows? It might’ve made you even bolder."
Lu Youqi gripped his belt, continuing his "fatherly education" in front of all his other sons.
By now, Lu Ludu had given up resisting, hanging silently—until he saw Lu Youqi’s gaze land on him."Pah!"
"What did you say?" Lu Youqi’s furious expression was genuinely terrifying.
"Lu! You! Qi! I despise you."
"You dare call me by my full name, you ungrateful wretch?" Lu Youqi was truly enraged.
Lu Ludu’s face twisted with hatred. "You hypocritical fraud. Every single one of us in the Lu Family—my siblings included—are nothing but tools for your gain."
His voice was weak, his body devoid of strength, but he wouldn’t die. Not because Lu Youqi held back out of love, but because this son still had uses.
"My greatest regret in life was being born into the Lu Family. Why didn’t you just strangle me at birth?"
Despair filled Lu Ludu’s heart.
Why bring me into this world? Why the Lu Family? And if you did, why abandon me?
Lu Ludu had never even met his mother—because no matter how many sons the Lu Family had, there could only be one official wife.
"And if you hadn’t made me seduce Luo Yao back then, would I have ended up like this?"
"Now that I’m no longer useful, you’re throwing me away?"
A bitter smile crept onto Lu Ludu’s face.
"Yes, I dealt drugs. Not just any drugs—I partnered with the biggest cartel. My goal was to make money and ruin you."
"You’re the person I hate most in this life."
The person he hated most was his own father?
Lu Ludu’s words even made Lu Youqi question himself.
"You vile creature! You still dare talk back?"
Lu Youqi didn’t hold back with the lashings. Lu Ludu’s body convulsed from the pain, but he clenched his teeth, refusing to beg for mercy.
"Speak, you brat! Say something!"
Lu Ludu forced out a ghastly grin.
"What’s there to say? Want me to confess? Forget it."
"If you’re so capable, find a scapegoat. But if you think handing me over will save the Lu Family, I’ll never admit to anything."
"No matter how many witnesses you produce, I won’t budge. Did you really think you’re the only one with connections? All these years, I’ve spent fortunes nurturing my own people. If anything happens to me, what do you think they’ll do?"
Lu Youqi hadn’t expected his own son to see through his plan so easily.
He had indeed intended to sacrifice Lu Ludu to bear the consequences.
A random scapegoat wouldn’t cut it—it wouldn’t convince anyone, not even himself.
Unless… it was a member of the Lu Family, and a direct descendant at that.
Lu Youqi narrowed his eyes. "You think you can play this game with me? Fine. I’ll show you what ‘forced confession’ really means."
Just as he prepared to continue, a subordinate rushed in with a report.
"Patriarch, it’s bad! The Lu Family’s drug dealings have been exposed. Not only is our port shut down, but all our subsidiaries are under siege. By tomorrow morning, our stock will plummet."
The subordinate merely stated facts. The Lu Family’s survival mattered to him, but not enough to stake his life on.
"The stock crash won’t destroy our foundation, but we’re in the middle of a bid. If this affects the outcome, securing future funding will become a problem—and the authorities will certainly take note."
"Plus, officials are already on their way. The entire Lu Family may be taken in for questioning."
Lu Youqi listened in shock, struggling to process the news.
"Luo Yao… you ruthless witch. Just you wait."
His gaze flicked back to Lu Ludu, who sneered.
"Oh? Is there something the great Patriarch Lu can’t handle?"
"Guards! Lock this wretch away. No one sees him without my permission."
"As for the investigation, cooperate fully. No resistance."
Once Lu Ludu was dragged off, Lu Youqi gathered his prized collection and left…
The current situation:
Samsung Group kept facing scandals, its stocks in freefall. Rumors spread that South Korea was entering an economic crisis, with countless citizens already standing on rooftops, awaiting their fate.
The Lu Family’s involvement in contraband had paralyzed their port—their most vital asset.
The exposure led to protests outside their subsidiaries, and partners were calling in the dead of night, demanding solutions or threatening to sever ties.
As for the Wang Family? Wang Dacong, the ultimate disgrace, had single-handedly become the internet’s newest meme icon.
You wouldn’t see him online, but his legend was everywhere.
The only one in the Tri-Alliance relatively unscathed was the Li Family.Google seaʀᴄh ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Many in the Li Family were practically worshipping Li Chifen—though he himself, while basking in the praise, couldn’t shake his unease.
But just because Luo Yao hadn’t targeted Li Chifen didn’t mean others wouldn’t.
Both the Lu and Wang Families had noticed something off about him.
"If we’re all in this alliance, why are you the only one untouched? If you’re not a mole, we’ll eat our hats."
So, before dawn even broke, the Li Family’s assets came under fire.
After all, an alliance meant sharing both fortune and misfortune, right?
And our protagonist? So far, he remained untouched.
By daybreak, two people awoke in the Stargazer’s Cave—once Luo Yao’s "home," now shared with another.
Truth be told, Lin Ran hadn’t slept well. Unlike Luo Yao, long accustomed to the place, he had… quirks.
No combat skills, no brains, no talent, no money—just a laundry list of flaws.
All he had was a handsome face and a soul devoted to Luo Yao.
But since when did protagonists have to be invincible?

chapters.title: Chapter 340
chapters.content:
Ordinary people can still be protagonists.
Or rather, everyone is the protagonist of their own world. We're all experiencing life for the first time—why not live it to the fullest?
Returning to the villa, the two had breakfast, and Liu Meng arrived for her routine report.
Time was running out—the 48-hour deadline Luo Yao had given was nearly up, and Liu Meng needed to pick up the pace.
After Liu Meng finished her report, Uncle Fu approached.
Jiang Feihua had grown increasingly irritated with Uncle Fu lately. The old man no longer showed the slightest respect for her as the estate manager.
Not only did he boss around the servants, but sometimes he even tried to give her orders, as if flaunting his authority.
This infuriated Jiang Feihua.
"Miss, Uncle Fu is getting old. Since he’s working so hard, perhaps he should take a break. I can take care of you and Young Master Lin during breakfast."
Lin Ran, Luo Yao, all the servants, and even Uncle Fu turned to stare at Jiang Feihua. No one expected the usually tactful Jiang Feihua to say something like this.Before anyone else could react, Lin Ran nodded.
"Sure, you can serve us then."
Jiang Feihua brightened at his words, but then froze, realizing what she had just done.
What had come over her?
Truly, jealousy was a monstrous thing—she desperately wanted to work closely with Luo Yao.
Uncle Fu said nothing, quietly stepping back.
He was more than happy to take it easy.
Jiang Feihua hurriedly explained, "I was just worried Uncle Fu might be overworked. He’s older, unlike me—I’m still young and full of energy..."
Luo Yao cut her off. "I don’t like unnecessary chatter during meals."
Jiang Feihua: ...
So all the sweet nothings you and Young Master Lin exchange aren’t considered nonsense?
Those meaningless romantic words—were those serious conversations?
Double standards.
But she kept these thoughts to herself, not daring to voice them.
"Yes," she replied, retreating to the side.
Lin Ran poked at his food a few times before setting down his chopsticks.
Jiang Feihua hesitated, unsure what to do.
"Did Uncle Fu ever tell you that our Yao Yao dislikes being disturbed during meals?"
Jiang Feihua: "Oh! Right, I’ll leave now."
She moved to stand with the other servants, her mood souring.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
Once breakfast ended, Luo Yao shot her a cold glance.
"Tomorrow, I don’t want to see A-Ran upset again."
Jiang Feihua broke into a cold sweat. Suddenly, serving the masters felt harder than ever.
It had always been challenging, but never this difficult.
Instead of heading to work, Luo Yao and Lin Ran relaxed in the living room.
"A-Ran, if you're tired, rest for a bit. Later, we’ll go watch the show."
Lin Ran sprawled across Luo Yao’s lap.
"I’ll sleep better like this."
Luo Yao smiled—Lin Ran was adorable like this.
And she had indeed changed recently. Uncle Fu wasn’t wrong; she knew it herself.
Maybe one day, she could grow old with Lin Ran like an ordinary couple.
What a lovely thought.
Of course, no matter how much she changed, Lin Ran belonged to her alone.
Anyone who dared stand in their way would meet a miserable end.
Like Liu Ruxue, like Huo Haini, like the three scum of the Liu family, like...
Meanwhile, in the capital...
Lin Jian stared at his phone in shock—every single order had been refunded.
A 100% return rate.
Not only was Lin Jian terrified, but his suppliers were even more panicked.
Forget production costs—just the shipping fees alone were a massive loss.
Now, customers wanted refunds, meaning return shipping costs and potential product damage.
Worst of all, this was a total loss with zero profit.
And even worse? The returned goods would likely end up as dead stock.
"That Lin Jian... I should’ve never worked with him. How much are we going to lose now?"
The brand owner checked the product reviews and nearly fainted.
[Cheering for Lin Jian]: Didn’t dare comment when ordering, just waiting for this moment—refund time!
[Who’s Born a Perfect Father?]: Let Lin Jian taste hope before despair.
[Master of the Onion Arts]: Looks like we all had the same idea. With 100K orders, we can’t afford to lose. Anyone who doesn’t refund? May your son be born without a—
The brand owner slammed his bowl of spicy noodles to the ground in fury.
Then he immediately called Lin Jian.
Lin Jian, seeing the caller ID, felt a chill.
"Ah, Boss Pei! What can I do for you? Need another collaboration?"
"Lin Jian, you absolute joke. You turned our products into a national boycott. Before working with you, we had sales. Now? We’re a laughingstock. And you dare mention collaboration? Are you out of your mind?"
Lin Jian knew the boss was losing money, but he blamed Lin Ran, not himself.
"Boss Pei, don’t worry. I know who’s behind this. Next time, I’ll fix it and boost sales."
"Fix your damn brain first! There won’t be a next time. Mark my words—I’ll ruin you, or my name isn’t Pei Deguang!"
Lin Jian, now threatened, scoffed.
"Calling you ‘boss’ is just courtesy. Without it, you’re nothing. Threaten me? Do you know how many followers I have?"
The other end went silent, utterly baffled by Lin Jian’s delusion.
What kind of idiot had he been to partner with this guy?
"You’re drowning in your own stupidity. ‘Followers’? You can’t even tell their true colors. Keep dreaming about being an influencer—you’re a damn joke!"
The call ended, leaving the boss fuming as he plotted revenge.
He picked up his phone again, dialing a friend...
With no sales, Lin Jian wouldn’t get his commission. Worse, he’d have to return the platform’s advance payments and face potential legal action from the brand.
"This is all Lin Ran’s fault!"
Furious, Lin Jian needed an outlet.
Once the harmless, meek boy of the Lin family, he was now its head—untouchable, doing as he pleased.
With a loud BANG, he kicked open the door to Lin Tianba and Liu Yuemei’s room.
The couple turned, startled.

chapters.title: Chapter 341
chapters.content:
Lin Jian had been treating them fairly well these past couple of days, especially Liu Yuemei. Though he had previously threatened to force her into prostitution, he ultimately let her off the hook because the goods were selling well.
Who would dare say Lin Jian wasn’t kind?
"Xiao Jian, how are the products selling? Did they blow up?"
The question came from Liu Yuemei, but Lin Tianba also pricked up his ears—Lin Jian’s success directly affected his quality of life.
And, more importantly, his pride.
He couldn’t even imagine the humiliation if Lin Jian actually made Liu Yuemei bring another man in front of him… Could he even endure it?
"Blew up? More like returned in droves."
"See, hubby? I told you our Xiao Jian would definitely sell out. Just as I expected, he— Wait, what did you say?"
Liu Yuemei suddenly processed Lin Jian’s words.
"I said the returns blew up. A hundred percent return rate.""How is that possible? Weren’t they all sold?"
Lin Jian walked up to Liu Yuemei, glanced at her, but chose not to lay a hand on her. Instead, he grabbed Lin Tianba by the hair.
"Old fool, it’s all your fault. Why did you have to give birth to someone like Lin Ran? Do you have any idea how many people are returning their purchases because of him? I lost a fortune this time, damn it!"
Lin Jian punched Lin Tianba square in the face.
Lin Tianba’s heart ached. He had completely lost hope in his son, but in this place, he couldn’t even argue back.
After all, his fate was in Lin Jian’s hands.
"Xiao Jian, take your dad to the hospital first. Once I recover, I’ll go out and earn money for you—even if I have to haul bricks to support you and your mother."
Lin Tianba spoke with genuine emotion, but Lin Jian had no intention of taking him to the hospital.
"Idiot. I’ll be going live later. Remember, act miserable, or I’ll make sure you end up completely useless."
"Okay, okay, I’ll act miserable. After the livestream, can you take me to the hospital?"
"We’ll see."
Lin Jian tossed the words over his shoulder and left.
The hospital? That would just cost more money.
What if you actually recover? Who’d I have left to milk for sympathy? You think I’m stupid?
Lin Tianba sighed.
"Ah! This is all because you spoiled him rotten."
The past few days had dealt him a heavy blow. He never imagined his beloved youngest son would turn out like this.
His eldest son had changed, and now his youngest had "changed" too. His heart was full of bitterness.
At least he still had his wife.
Slap! Liu Yuemei struck Lin Tianba across the face.
"Now you’re just a useless waste. You only get food because of me, and you still dare to boss me around?"
Liu Yuemei wasn’t afraid in the slightest—Lin Tianba no longer had the strength to hit her.
Lin Tianba: "..."
"Wah… You’ve changed too."
In Shanghai, Lin Ran slowly woke up to find Luo Yao gently stroking his cheek.
"Sorry about that, wifey. Your lap was so comfortable I dozed off."
Luo Yao continued caressing his face as she spoke.
"It’s fine. I liked it. For a moment, I really wished you’d never wake up—just stay like this, quietly by my side."
There had even been a fleeting thought of ending Lin Ran right then and there, keeping him frozen in that position forever.
But the idea of him never speaking again, never calling her "wifey," never smiling at her… she couldn’t bring herself to do it.
"Huh? That’s a bit much. If I never woke up, who’d cook for you? Who’d whisper sweet nothings? Who’d make you happy?"
"Exactly. That’s why I spared you. Remember, A’Ran, the only reason you’re alive isn’t luck—it’s because I’ve let you live, over and over. If I hadn’t, you’d have been done for the day you rejected me."
There was no denying that. Lin Ran didn’t argue.
"True. Thanks for sparing me, Your Majesty."
Noticing Luo Yao still hadn’t moved, Lin Ran asked,
"Didn’t you say you’d take me to see a show today? When are we leaving?"ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ
"Soon. We’ll go once Liu Meng gets here."
Speak of the devil—Liu Meng walked in.
"President Luo, Li Chifen has invited you to the Li Family Estate."
Luo Yao: "Since when do random strays dare invite me?"
Lin Ran: "Yeah, what’s the point of going?"
Liu Meng’s face darkened. The Li Family was far from insignificant—in many industries, they were considered top-tier.
"The Lu and Wang Families have already started targeting the Li Family. I suspect he’s feeling the pressure and wants to surrender."
Disdain filled Luo Yao’s eyes. "He’s not worthy. I said he’d die, and he will."
"A’Ran and I are heading to the restaurant first. I’ll personally enjoy his final act later."
Liu Meng nodded and left. She knew her time was running short, but everything was proceeding smoothly.
The mission was already 75% complete—the only thing left was the Li Family.
She made a call to Li Chifen. No one knew what was said.
Hanging up, Liu Meng’s eyes gleamed with confidence.
"Before dealing with the Li Family, it’s necessary to mess with the Wang and Lu Families a little."
Ten minutes later, the Li Family abruptly announced their withdrawal from the tri-family alliance and the joint bid with Samsung.
The news sent shockwaves not only through the South China Chamber of Commerce but also through their three partners.
The Li Family wasn’t some minor collaborator—they were the core of this bidding project.
The two families and Samsung’s Park Bo-gi immediately convened to address the crisis.
Lu Youqi was livid.
"What the hell is he playing at? Even if we’re at odds, he can’t just abandon the family’s interests like this! I knew it—that bastard is Luo Yao’s mole!"
Wang Xiaolin was also struggling to breathe. He had invested too much in this bid.
Now, with the project stalled and the Li Family’s betrayal, his own business was paralyzed.
"Ugh… I don’t know if I’ll survive this."
He was already considering whether to beg Luo Yao for mercy.
But remembering her ruthless methods, he hesitated.
Park Bo-gi was equally overwhelmed.
"Patriarch Lu, if we win the bid, the Li Family will regret their withdrawal. But I need to know—if we succeed, what happens to the funds they already invested?"
The final decision: the bid must proceed. The three would pool resources to cover the Li Family’s share and seek new partners.
The announcement sent tremors through the business world.
While handling their own crises, the Lu and Wang Families also seized every chance to suppress the Li Family.
The rift between them was now irreparable.
Yet, Li Chifen, the patriarch of the Li Family, remained unshaken, as calm as a mountain breeze.
"Everyone says the Li Family can’t compare to the Lu Family. This time, I’ll show them which of the three great families of Shanghai truly reigns supreme."
His phone rang. Glancing at the screen, Li Chifen answered with confidence.
"Peace Restaurant? Got it. I’ll be there."

chapters.title: Chapter 342
chapters.content:
An hour later...
At the Peace Hotel in Shanghai.
This was a historic hotel that had stood since the wartime era. During the turbulent years of China's past, many influential figures had gathered here to discuss matters. Even now, in the new era, the tradition remained—a mark of respect for history.
No one knew who the current owner of the Peace Hotel was, but no one dared to cause trouble either. There was simply no need.
Liu Meng had arranged a meeting with the representatives of the three major families—all except the Samsungs.
Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin had already arrived and were seated in Private Room No. 1, their expressions grim. The two of them had been pushed to the brink by Liu Meng’s maneuvers. The moment she entered the room, their eyes immediately darted behind her.
But there were only two assistants, carrying a few documents.
"Where’s President Luo?"
Liu Meng strode straight to the head of the table and sat down without hesitation, a move that visibly angered the two tycoons.
"President Luo won’t be joining us today. I’m the one who called this meeting."The two men exchanged glances.
"Hmph! Even Luo Yao would have to ask for our permission before sitting there. Who the hell do you think you are?"
Liu Meng tossed two stacks of documents onto the table.
"Save the bravado. Take a look at these acquisition proposals."
"Acquisition proposals?"
What the hell?
Confused, they picked up the documents. By the time they finished the first page, their eyes had widened in shock.
"What? You want to buy out all our businesses? This is outrageous! Since when did Luo Yao develop such an appetite?"
Wang Xiaolin, however, remained silent.
While the terms were far from favorable for him, he couldn’t deny that the proposal offered a way to cut his losses and survive. The only catch was the acquisition method—Luo Corporation demanded absolute control despite holding a minority stake.
Narrowing his eyes, Wang Xiaolin spotted the loophole.
Luo Corporation had always been known for its deep pockets, so why resort to such underhanded tactics instead of a straightforward buyout?
It could be Luo Yao’s shrewd business tactics—or it could mean Luo Corporation was strapped for cash.
"Tch." Wang Xiaolin sighed.
Even if Luo Corporation was financially strained, what could he do about it?
He had long wanted to take down Luo Corporation, especially in recent days. He believed Luo Yao was engaging in cutthroat competition—if that was the game, then no one would come out unscathed.
But guess what?
No matter how hard he and Lu Youqi dug, they couldn’t find a single scandal tied to Luo Corporation. Every operation was squeaky clean.
For a conglomerate of this scale—the world’s top financial empire—to maintain such integrity wasn’t just difficult; it was nearly impossible.
Lu Youqi had once suggested spreading false rumors, but before they could act, the plan backfired spectacularly.
Now, even if they tried again, it wouldn’t matter. Lies were still lies.
At best, it might tarnish Luo Yao’s reputation slightly, but it wouldn’t disqualify her from the bidding war.
Wang Xiaolin’s understanding of Luo Yao had deepened.
Liu Meng: "If you two aren’t interested, then so be it. We’ll keep playing hardball. But just remember—going head-to-head with Luo Corporation means risking total annihilation."
Lu Youqi finally snapped. His usual composed demeanor vanished, replaced by a furious glare.
"You little bitch, do you really think I’ll let you walk out of this hotel alive?"
Liu Meng clapped her hands mockingly. "Calm down, Patriarch Lu. Whether I leave here or not isn’t up to you."
At that moment, the hotel’s elite security team stormed in. Liu Meng leaned back lazily.
"This hotel isn’t yours to command."
Lu Youqi’s eyes bulged in disbelief.
"What? The owner here is… Luo Corporation?"
Liu Meng shook her head. "To be precise, it belongs to our young master, Lin Ran."
The two men fell silent for a long moment before finally speaking.
"Even so, we won’t agree."
Liu Meng didn’t argue.
"Agreement isn’t the point. Actually, today, I wanted to show you a little spectacle."
"What spectacle?"
"The downfall of the Li family."
Both men stared at her, unable to believe an assistant could be so audacious.
Even if they joined forces, they could only deal a minor blow to the Li family. Total annihilation?
"Hahaha! I’ve seen arrogance, but never like this."
Liu Meng shrugged. "Well, today’s your lucky day."
"Fine, fine. Let’s see how the Li family falls. How long do you need to pull it off?"
Liu Meng held up one finger. Lu Youqi frowned.
"A year? A month?"
Liu Meng shook her head.
Wang Xiaolin: "Don’t tell me it’s just one day?"
Again, Liu Meng shook her head. "One hour."
The two men were speechless…
"Haha, my apologies for being late!" Li Chifen strode in, head held high, nodding only at Liu Meng.
Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin could only gape at Li Chifen, then back at Liu Meng, utterly baffled by whatever game they were playing…
Meanwhile, upstairs, Luo Yao and Lin Ran gazed at the Bund’s skyline, awaiting the outcome.
"Yao Yao, is this hotel really mine? It’s such an iconic place."
The Peace Hotel wasn’t particularly large or luxurious, but its legacy was undeniable—a century-old institution, even designated as a cultural heritage site.
"It’s just a hotel. If you like it, keep it. If not, I’ll have it burned down."
Lin Ran sweatdropped. This woman was unbelievable.
A historic landmark, and she talked about torching it like it was nothing.
Was money really that trivial to her?
"That won’t be necessary. It may not be a five-star hotel, but it’s got character. And it’s a state-protected heritage site—how did you even manage this?"ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
"I traded a project for it. But that’s irrelevant. What matters is that you’re happy."
Even after all this time, Lin Ran was still moved by Luo Yao’s devotion.
This level of pampering was reserved for him alone.
He could only imagine how significant that "project" must have been.
"Ran, what do you think will happen to the Li family this time?"
Lin Ran thought back to his past life. Something felt off.
In that timeline, the Li family had also collapsed—but not this soon.
It had happened much later. Yet now, the process had accelerated.
Was this another ripple effect?
Well, it didn’t concern him.
"I’d say the Li family is about to become history."
Luo Yao blinked.
"Then shouldn’t we celebrate this historic moment?"

chapters.title: Chapter 343
chapters.content:
"How should we celebrate?"
"The relatives have left."
Lin Ran lowered her head.
The view from the Bund was stunning, casting a particularly beautiful reflection through the window.
This was a moment of brilliance reserved solely for the two of them.
Romantic and moving...
"Ah Ran, let’s enjoy watching Old Li’s downfall now."ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
"Alright."
Luo Yao particularly disliked Li Chifen—not because of business matters or his past condescending attitude toward her.
It was solely because Li Chifen had disrespected Lin Ran at the last banquet.Luo Yao had let it slide then, but that didn’t mean she’d let it go forever.
Now, it was time to avenge her man.
Her man was hers to tease—no one else had the right. Anyone who dared cross that line had "already signed their own death warrant."
That was also why Luo Yao had handed the evidence to Liu Meng. She wanted to push Liu Meng to grow while delivering a crushing blow to the Li Family—one that would wipe them out completely.
Downstairs, the heads of the three major families stared at Liu Meng, utterly baffled.
Li Chifen wondered why Liu Meng had invited all three of them.
Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin, on the other hand, were thinking, "Wasn’t the plan to destroy the Li Family? Why is he here?"
"I know you must have questions, but don’t worry. Just watch the news in a moment."
With that, Liu Meng sent a message from her phone.
[Execute.]
At the same time, Luo Corporation filed a formal report accusing the Li father and son of treason.
They had sold core national technology to foreign entities.
Not only that, they had also leaked massive amounts of Chinese client data—undeniable acts of betrayal.
The news was explosive.
It was as if we’d discovered that Jack Ma had handed over Alipay’s user data to foreigners while funding weapons to turn against us.
Or like Siemens docking Japanese warships at Tokyo Harbor, aiming their guns at Japan itself.
The public was sent into an uproar.
Lu, Li, and Wang were stunned as they read the headlines.
Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin turned to Li Chifen in shock.
"Li Chifen, how dare you?" They couldn’t believe it.
Li Chifen’s breathing grew heavy. "Assistant Liu, what is the meaning of this? Weren’t we supposed to be collaborating?"
"When did I say that? Show me proof." Liu Meng feigned ignorance, picking at her ear.
Realizing he’d been played, Li Chifen’s face darkened.
"So this was your plan all along? You never intended to let me live?"
Liu Meng raised an eyebrow. "Already cracking? Don’t worry, it’s not over yet."
The three men froze.
There was more?
Liu Meng tossed a tablet onto the untouched round dining table.
It displayed footage of arrests—though the criminals wore hoods, the background unmistakably showed the Li Family estate.
A reporter was speaking confidently.
"According to Luo Corporation’s report, the Li Family of Shanghai exploited their influence in the entertainment industry to organize prostitution rings, forming a full-fledged operation."
"Li Chifen and his father have already been arrested for treason. This case involves numerous individuals—we will neither wrong the innocent nor spare the guilty."
"Additionally, evidence provided by Luo Corporation has uncovered a child trafficking ring. Some of these abducted children were groomed by the Li Family for illegal profits, while others remain missing. Multiple Li Family members are implicated… Per official request, this station will continue reporting updates, ensuring full transparency."
This time, Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin weren’t just shocked—they were dumbfounded.
Prostitution rings were one thing—they’d known about that—but child trafficking?
Wang Xiaolin frowned. "Wait, the news says the Li father and son have been arrested. So who’s standing in front of us?"
Liu Meng smirked. "Just wait."
Li Chifen’s expression turned murderous. "Liu Meng, I’ll kill you—"
Suddenly, the private room door burst open. Armed officers swarmed in, pinning Li Chifen to the ground.
"Freeze!"
Li Chifen was dragged away before he could even resist.
Before leaving, the lead officer gave Liu Meng a nod.
"Thank you, Luo Corporation, for your report and cooperation in apprehending the suspect. We’ll take him now."
Liu Meng nodded. She knew exactly what awaited Li Chifen.
China had zero tolerance for traitors.
Spies were usually secretly transported to Beijing, locked away for life.
But Li Chifen’s crimes went beyond treason.
He had orchestrated prostitution rings involving his artists—a scheme many might dismiss as minor, but in reality, it was how the Li Family expanded their connections.
The clients weren’t ordinary people. Countless high-profile protectors would likely be exposed.
Even Lu Youqi had indulged in these services.
But the most horrifying revelation was the child trafficking. No one could’ve imagined such darkness behind the Li Family’s glamorous facade.
The news mentioned many missing children—their fates unimaginable.
After the officers left, Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin studied Liu Meng with newfound gravity.
"Don’t look at me. The show’s over. Have you two made your decision?"
After a long silence, Lu Youqi spoke first.
"One question—how did you uncover all this? And how did Li Chifen remain completely unaware?"
"I shouldn’t explain, but I’ll humor you. When I targeted the Lu and Wang Families but spared the Li Family, you figured it out—I wanted you to turn on each other."
"While you kept harassing him, I dangled empty promises from Luo Corporation. Li Chifen, torn between panic and excitement, had no time to notice the trap."
"Even his arrest here was part of the plan—just so you could witness it firsthand."
Liu Meng’s tone was calm, as if she hadn’t orchestrated the entire scheme.
But Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin were anything but calm. Their minds reeled.
Especially Wang Xiaolin—he saw the bigger picture.
Bringing down the Li Family seemed straightforward, but the execution was anything but.
Precise, ruthless, and airtight—no room for reversal.
Luo Yao had ensured the Li Family’s annihilation.
Liu Meng checked her watch, a slow smile forming.
48 hours—right on schedule.
All three families had been brought to their knees.

chapters.title: Chapter 344
chapters.content:
"Since you haven't made up your minds yet, I won’t disturb the two family heads any longer. I hope you won’t make decisions you’ll regret."
Liu Meng had no intention of waiting any longer. The seeds had already been sown, and the harvest would come sooner or later.
"Wait—you still haven’t told us how you uncovered the Li Family’s misdeeds. And how did you know about the Lu Family’s affairs?"
One could say Liu Meng’s dismantling of the three major families felt almost like a joke.
It was as if she barely lifted a finger, and their empires crumbled like rotten wood.
These were the three major families, not some small-time businesses.
"What I just said was giving you half a face—that’s all I can reveal. But as they say, the innocent have nothing to fear. If you hadn’t done those things, I wouldn’t have been able to exploit them. Isn’t that right, Lu Youqi?"
Lu Youqi gritted his teeth, saying nothing. Though he wouldn’t admit it aloud, he had already acknowledged Luo Yao’s ruthlessness—her methods were even more brutal than before.
Wang Xiaolin sighed. "President Luo is truly formidable. Who would’ve thought? I, Wang Xiaolin, who’ve scaled the heights and plunged into the abyss, would end up defeated by a mere girl."
Luo Yao was only 26 years old, so calling her a "girl" wasn’t wrong. But Liu Meng couldn’t stand it. "There’s one more thing you should know. President Luo gave me 48 hours to bring your three families to a standstill. The time’s just up—mission accomplished."Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin stared at Liu Meng in shock.
"So… all of this was your doing?"
Liu Meng nodded. "To be precise, it was accomplished under President Luo’s support."
The two exchanged glances, seeing the same disbelief in each other’s eyes.
"Kids these days… they really don’t know restraint," Lu Youqi grumbled.
"But heroes do emerge from the young," Wang Xiaolin admitted sincerely.
"That’s not the point. What I’m telling you is—you should be grateful President Luo handed this task to me. If she had taken action herself, whether you’d still be standing here right now would be anyone’s guess."
"So, the true extent of President Luo’s capabilities? You haven’t even glimpsed them. She’s no ‘girl’—she’s a bona fide demon queen."
The two fell silent, but the tremor in their hearts was unmistakable.
Before leaving the private room, Liu Meng turned back. "Oh, one more thing. President Luo said since you’ve offended our Young Master Lin, if you agree to our acquisition proposal, you’ll have to kneel and apologize to him in person."
With that, Liu Meng left—swaggering out without a care.
"Did we even offend Lin Ran?"
"All I did was exchange a few words with him. He even threatened to burn down the Lu Family estate—and that counts as an offense?"
Wang Xiaolin gave a bitter laugh. "At least you had a reason. I can’t even figure out why I’m involved."
"Ugh." Lu Youqi sighed. Truthfully, he was exhausted.
The night before, he had personally undergone official questioning. Now, even his movements were restricted—the authorities had ordered all direct descendants of the Lu Family to remain in Shanghai.
Even when he tried calling in favors, doors were slammed in his face. Those people had taken plenty from Lu Youqi in the past, yet now they didn’t dare lift a finger to help him.
It felt like the Lu Family’s entire network of influence had snapped like a frayed rope, useless when it mattered most.
And right at this moment, Liu Meng had completed the 48-hour mission Luo Yao had assigned her.
The stocks of the three major families plummeted, leaving countless investors wailing in despair.
Without Li Chifen at the helm, the rest of the Li Family had become frightened birds, easily startled.
Almost all direct descendants had been taken away, leaving the collateral branches powerless—without even the authority to make decisions.
Of course, an empire this large couldn’t collapse overnight. The authorities, as the Li Family’s former largest partner, stepped in to temporarily take over operations.
Temporary management—not absorption or nationalization. Doing otherwise would make it seem like the government was just after profit.
If that happened, who would dare cooperate with the authorities in the future?
Meanwhile, Lin Ran and Luo Yao had already finished their discussion just as Liu Meng arrived outside the door.
A knock. Luo Yao permitted her entry.
"This mission was… passable."
A single sentence from Luo Yao sent Liu Meng’s mind reeling.
On the surface, it seemed simple, but it was Luo Yao’s acknowledgment—her approval.
This meant Liu Meng’s future in Luo Corporation held the potential for even greater advancement.
Though her official rank hadn’t surpassed certain executives, within the company, she was already second only to one.
One more step, and she’d be…
Liu Meng didn’t dare imagine further.
Lin Ran gave a slight nod.
He knew Liu Meng would soon become Luo Corporation’s de facto second-in-command.
In the previous life, she had achieved it. In this one, she would again.
Only this time, the timeline had been pushed forward considerably.
Back at Peace Hotel, Lu Youqi and Wang Xiaolin still hadn’t recovered from the shock.
"That woman, Luo Yao… she’s no ordinary opponent," Lu Youqi finally conceded, his admiration laced with dread.
"But if she thinks I, Lu Youqi, will just roll over, she’s sorely mistaken."
Wang Xiaolin stayed silent. In truth, his resolve was wavering.
He had grown weary over the years.
Perhaps handing his doomed empire to someone capable wasn’t such a bad idea.
He had two sons.
One was named Wang Dacong.
The other was named Doomed Enterprises.
"Family Head Lu, what’s your next move?"
"I’ll invite Luo Yao to the Lu Family estate as a guest. Maybe we can ease tensions—keep our wells from mixing."
The bidding for the tech city no longer mattered. Luo Yao wanted their submission.
Lu Youqi, proud for half a lifetime—how could he accept that?
"Alright. I’ll wait for your good news."
Lu Youqi shot Wang Xiaolin a look. "You’re not actually considering surrendering to Luo Yao, are you?"
"Impossible. Do I look like someone who’d trade integrity for profit? You know my principles, old friend."
"Good."
At the same time, in the Shanghai branch of the National Academy of Sciences, Chen Buhui narrowed his eyes.
"I’m no businessman. Commercial competition isn’t my domain, nor do I have the authority to intervene."
"But Luo Yao’s methods… I find them deeply distasteful. Frankly, I despise them."
"Luo Corporation’s ruthless tactics have laid bare their merciless nature."
The other experts remained silent. They cared little for corporate battles.
Their only concern was which proposal best suited the future tech city.
This was a government-mandated, high-priority project.
If not for recent budget constraints and gaps in core technologies, there’d be no need for bidding at all.
Besides, most here didn’t see Luo Yao as being in the wrong. She had, after all, exposed traitors.
Where was the mistake?
"Arrange a meeting. Tell them Chen Buhui demands their presence." He pointed at himself with his thumb.

chapters.title: Chapter 345
chapters.content:
Everyone turned their heads in confusion, unable to understand why Chen Buhui wanted to meet these two people privately—it went against protocol.
Moreover, if word got out, it would send a signal to the outside world.
Even though the three major families had collapsed, there was still the South China Chamber of Commerce among the bidding candidates.
But faced with a heavyweight like Chen Buhui, no one dared to oppose outright—they could only try to persuade her gently.
"Elder Chen, isn’t this a bit inappropriate?"
"There’s nothing inappropriate about it. After all, I don’t control the final bidding results, and I’ll avoid dealing with these businessmen afterward. The reason I called them here is simply to chat and teach them how to behave."
Everyone fell silent.
When it came to scientific contributions, Chen Buhui’s achievements were indeed significant, and the authorities went out of their way to protect her.
But as a person? She was practically useless.
She had offended more than a few people.And no matter who she was dealing with, she always acted like a teacher, lecturing anyone she disapproved of—regardless of their industry or whether they were in research.
Ah, well. Who could argue with a big shot like her?
By the time Lin Ran and Luo Yao returned to the villa estate, the direction of the bidding had become clear.
Now, their only remaining opponent was the South China Chamber of Commerce.
But just as Luo Yao had predicted, internal problems had begun surfacing within the Chamber. The specifics didn’t matter enough to waste words on.
The real reason was that the allied companies were terrified of Luo Yao.
Faced with the madwoman who had brought down the three major families, everyone was on edge.
So, let’s focus on the daily lives of our protagonists instead.
On the way back to the estate, Lin Ran, ever the gossip lover, pulled out his phone to check online reactions.
【Two Purple Grapes】: At this point, I’m convinced Luo Yao was behind the downfall of the three families. Terrifying.
【Li Chifen Backwards】: Why blame Luo Yao the moment something happens? If they hadn’t done those things, how could she have exploited them? Support Luo Corporation—the Li family deserves a thousand cuts.
【World, Just End Already】: This is insane. The Lu family smuggled and dealt drugs, the Li family organized prostitution, child trafficking, and treason, and the Wang family evaded taxes while their disgraceful son became a teacher… Every single one of these scandals is explosive. I’ve been binge-reading gossip nonstop these past two days.
【Speechless People Just Laugh】: I don’t even know what to say. I know Luo Yao wasn’t wrong, but I still feel physically uncomfortable. Of course, my soul is even more disturbed by what actually happened. Is this what the world is really like? Why does it feel like I’ve never known it at all?
Putting his phone down, Lin Ran let out a bitter chuckle.
"From today onward, you’re officially the world’s greatest villain in their eyes."
"And what am I in yours?"
"In my eyes, you’re the most beautiful angel."
Liu Meng lowered her head, lips moving in a silent mutter.
"Oho, the most beautiful angel…"
Luo Yao: "What are you mumbling about?"
Liu Meng: "Huh? I—I didn’t say anything."
Shortly after returning to the estate, Liu Meng received updates and reported them to Luo Yao.
"President Luo, Lu Youqi, the head of the Lu family, has invited you and Young Master Lin to the Lu estate for tea."
"President Luo, Chen Buhui from the Chinese Academy of Sciences has also invited you and Young Master Lin to the Shanghai branch for tea."
"President Luo, representatives from the South China Chamber of Commerce have invited you to their temporary alliance headquarters for tea."
Luo Yao’s expression turned icy.
"Do I look like someone who enjoys tea?"
Lin Ran, massaging her legs, chimed in, "These people are a mixed bag—who knows if they’re good or bad? I don’t think we should go."
Luo Yao: "Hear that? A-Ran has spoken. Reject them. If they invite us again, don’t even report it to me—just refuse outright. Tell them if they have business, they can come to the estate and pay their respects. I won’t go to them."
"Because they’re not worthy."
Lin Ran backed his wife up. "Exactly. Who do they think we are? Just because they invite us, we’ll go? Are our feet worthless or something? Wait—actually, why would they invite me? It makes sense for Yao Yao, but what do they want with me?"
Liu Meng replied matter-of-factly, "You’re our boss’s husband—the palanquin bearer in President Luo’s hands. Who would dare overlook you?"
Luo Yao gave Liu Meng a surprised glance.
"You’ve suddenly become eloquent. Keep it up."
Suddenly, Lin Ran frowned.
"Wait, who did you say invited us? Isn’t Chen Buhui Elder Chen?"
Luo Yao’s eyes flicked toward him. "You want to go?"
"No, but isn’t Chen Buhui the organizer of this bidding process? Is it really okay to refuse like this?"
"The government is the organizer. Chen Buhui is just their representative. If it weren’t her, someone else would be. Zhang San could represent them, Li Si could too—don’t think anyone is irreplaceable."
Lin Ran gazed at Luo Yao intently. "In my world, you’re irreplaceable."
Moved to tears, Luo Yao responded with a passionate kiss.
Liu Meng waited until they were done before speaking up. "Miss, brushing off others is one thing, but with Chen Buhui… Wouldn’t our response seem disrespectful to the government?"
Lin Ran actually agreed—after all, Chen Buhui represented the authorities.
"Respect? If the Chinese Academy of Sciences invited us, I might grant that respect. But you said it yourself—it’s Chen Buhui of the Academy inviting us. That’s a personal request. Why should I humor her?"
Luo Yao’s logic was airtight, leaving even Lin Ran momentarily speechless.
Noticing his silence, Luo Yao added, "A-Ran, actually, Chen Buhui has some connection to you."
Lin Ran blinked. "What, is she from the Chen family too?"
Luo Yao nodded.
"Yes. But I don’t like her, and I don’t want you to meet her—because it would make you unhappy."
"Why?"
"Because she loves lecturing people. You’re my husband. No one but me gets to lecture you."
Lin Ran laughed and shook his head. "So that’s the only reason you don’t want to go? That’s my wife for you."
"Mm!"
Lin Ran sighed. "Sometimes I really admire these elders—thinking their age gives them the right to lecture others, never considering whether people want to hear it."
"Honestly, they’re exhausting. Not that I deny their past achievements, but that doesn’t make them entitled to preach."
He knew if he voiced these thoughts publicly, he’d be met with a storm of criticism. But this was how he truly felt.
"A-Ran, I love this side of you. So let’s not meet them, okay?"
Lin Ran flashed an OK sign. "Deal. No meetings, no lectures."
Little did they know—while they avoided Chen Buhui, she would soon come to them herself, ready to unleash her full force.
"Miss, how many more days until we return to the capital?"

chapters.title: Chapter 346
chapters.content:
Taking advantage of Jiang Feihua's absence, Uncle Fu posed the question.
Luo Yao glanced at him.
"What, eager to go back and spend time with your grandson?"
Uncle Fu didn’t deny it—that was exactly what he had in mind.
"An Jian’s surgery is coming up soon, and I’d like to be there for Dahua. If you still need me here, I’d like to request leave for that day."
Uncle Fu had braced himself for a pay cut, but to his surprise, Luo Yao nodded.
"If that’s what you wish, I won’t stop you. If I recall correctly, your grandson’s surgery is in four days. Barring any unexpected issues, we’ll make it back in time."
Uncle Fu’s eyes widened in disbelief.
"We?"
Lin Ran chuckled and patted Uncle Fu’s shoulder."Old man, I already talked to Yao Yao about this. See how good I am to you? So, no more badmouthing me behind my back, got it?"
Uncle Fu was genuinely moved.
"When have I ever badmouthed you? I never gossip about people behind their backs."
Lin Ran smirked. "Oh really? Even when you said that if I fed Miss Luo—"
Uncle Fu hastily clapped a hand over Lin Ran’s mouth, his face a picture of panic.
Luo Yao narrowed her eyes at him. "You didn’t actually say something bad about me in front of A-Ran, did you?"
Uncle Fu immediately looked crestfallen. "Miss, I’d never dare! It was just a slip of the tongue—I said that even if Young Master Lin fed you poison, you’d drink it without hesitation."
Luo Yao nodded. "That’s true enough."
Lin Ran gave Uncle Fu a strange look, silently noting that he’d left something out.
"Yao Yao, if I really fed you poison, would you drink it?"
Luo Yao answered as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
"Of course."
"Why?"
"Because A-Ran wanted me to."
Lin Ran was at a loss for words. He stiffly asked,
"Then… would you really be willing to leave me?"
Luo Yao shook her head firmly.
"Of course not. Don’t worry—you won’t leave me. If I drank poison and was going to die, I’d make sure to take you with me first. That way, even in the afterlife, you’d still be mine. We’d never be apart."
Lin Ran’s heart gave a little shudder.The source of thɪs content is ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Luo Yao continued, elaborating on her thoughts.
"And after we die, someone will bury us together, so we’ll never be separated for all eternity. Right, Uncle Fu?"
Uncle Fu wiped the sweat from his brow. Even after all these years as Luo Yao’s butler, he still struggled to follow her logic.
Especially when it came to Lin Ran—why did she always have such extreme ideas?
Thankfully, Wang Dahua didn’t have such a terrifying possessiveness toward him.
Otherwise, he wasn’t sure his old bones could withstand that kind of "love."
"Of course. This old servant will ensure that Miss… and Young Master Lin receive the most proper funeral arrangements."
Lin Ran had felt a brief tremor at Luo Yao and Uncle Fu’s conversation, but he quickly brushed it off.
There was nothing wrong with Luo Yao’s plan to take him with her if she died.
That was true love—together in life, together in death.
And Uncle Fu? Well, he’d already proven he could handle their funeral arrangements.
But now—
"I don’t want that."
Luo Yao’s expression instantly turned icy, her gaze sharp as a blade. Even Uncle Fu frowned.
Uncle Fu thought to himself, "Young Master Lin always says he has a death wish, but it seems like you’re the one courting death here."
Lin Ran shook his head. "I don’t want Yao Yao to drink poison, and I don’t want to die. We can be the happiest couple in the world while we’re alive—why think about death?"
"The thought of Yao Yao collapsing makes me feel like I’m suffocating. I’d never let Yao Yao die, and I’d never make her unhappy. I only want her to feel my love."
Uncle Fu was impressed. "Well played," he mused. "Young Master Lin, you’re truly a master of wordplay."
"A-Ran, I want to devour you."
Lin Ran: "…Huh?"
Uncle Fu: "Everyone, clear out."
While Luo Yao and Lin Ran were… deepening their bond, the Lu Family, the Southern China Chamber of Commerce, and Chen Buhui all received the news that Luo Yao had refused to meet.
Their reactions varied—some were furious, some silent, others indifferent.
Lu Youqi was the angriest. Outwardly refined and composed, he was a raging tyrant within the walls of the Lu estate when no outsiders were around.
Among the three great families, the most level-headed was actually the least conspicuous—Wang Xiaolin.
The Southern China Chamber of Commerce didn’t care much. They’d only invited Luo Yao to foster goodwill and avoid cutthroat competition.
But deep down, they lacked confidence in their own position.
Chen Buhui remained silent, thinking to herself, "These youngsters don’t know their place." Aloud, she said, "They’re rather arrogant, aren’t they?"
"Elder Chen, if they don’t want to meet, we shouldn’t force it. After all, we’re here on official business."
Chen Buhui shook her head, her gaze unfriendly.
"Refusing to see their elder? Fine. Very well. Then I’ll go to them."
The others exchanged surprised glances. They didn’t understand why Chen Buhui was so insistent on meeting these two.
Weren’t they just here to fulfill an official assignment? There was no need to take it so personally.
No matter who secured the project, it would benefit the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
"Elder Chen, you—"
"It’s fine. I’m going in a personal capacity—this has nothing to do with the Academy. Arrange a car for me."
Chen Buhui had one defining trait—she hated waiting. If something could be done, she did it immediately.
"Very well." Her assistant sighed and went to make arrangements. After all, this was Elder Chen.
When Chen Buhui arrived at the estate, even she was stunned by its opulence.
Despite being a leading figure in science, she lived in a modest 100-square-meter house. In contrast, Lin Ran and Luo Yao resided in a lavish estate—and this wasn’t even their primary residence, just a temporary dwelling.
At that moment, Chen Buhui’s dislike for Luo Yao and Lin Ran’s extravagance grew, but so did her understanding of the First Financial Consortium’s staggering wealth.
"Extravagant. Wasteful." That was her blunt four-word verdict.
The security at the gate stopped them.
"Who are you here to see?"
The driver, also her assistant, was a young woman who held a minor role at the Academy.
"This is Elder Chen Buhui. We’re here to see Luo Yao and Lin Ran."
The guard glanced inside, confirming the stern-faced woman was indeed Chen Buhui.
"Do you have an appointment?"
Chen Buhui finally lost her patience.
"I need an appointment to see them?"
The guard knew her status and remained respectful, but he was just doing his job.
"Apologies, but countless people come here daily hoping to meet Miss Luo and Young Master Lin. Without an appointment, no one gets in—no exceptions."

chapters.title: Chapter 347
chapters.content:
Chen Buhui was so furious she nearly keeled over.
"Quite the little capitalist at such a young age, aren’t you?"
"Tell them Chen Buhui is here to visit, and they’d better come out to greet me personally." Chen Buhui jabbed her thumb backward at her own face, as if it were some kind of VIP pass valid across all of China.
The security guard frowned. He hated that gesture, but since it was Chen Buhui, he held his tongue and relayed the message over his walkie-talkie.
They waited, but no response came.
"Base to HQ, come in."
"Miss Luo and Young Master Lin are... busy bonding. Whatever it is, it can wait."
The reply crackled through the earpiece, leaving the guard no choice but to relay the message to Chen Buhui.
"Our young lady and Young Master Lin are occupied at the moment. We can’t interrupt. Would you like to wait or come back another time?"
Chen Buhui took a deep breath."I, Chen Buhui, demand to see them, and instead of rushing out to greet me, they make me wait? Who do they think I am?"Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn
The guard offered an apologetic smile. "Sorry, but without permission, I really can’t let you in."
Chen Buhui’s patience had run out.
"Liu! We’re barging in. Let’s see what’s so important they can’t be bothered."
The guard narrowed his eyes and spoke into his earpiece.
"Intruder attempting to breach the estate. All units, stand by."
He drew his weapon, and within moments, over a dozen guards assembled, forming a human barricade at the entrance.
Chen Buhui froze at the sight.
"This is China, not some playground for reckless youngsters. I advise you to lower your weapons and not stray onto the path of crime. What you’re doing is illegal."
The guard dropped the polite act.
"We haven’t done anything. And even if we did, you’d be the one at fault. This is private property. Forcing your way in counts as trespassing—so who’s breaking the law here?"
It baffled the guard that someone as high-profile as Chen Buhui could be so legally clueless.
Chen Buhui’s face darkened. She never expected Luo Yao’s people to be this bold.
"Do you even know who I am?"
"Yes, Chen Buhui. You’ve mentioned."
"I’m an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. You dare block me?" Chen Buhui had no choice but to pull rank.
The guard didn’t budge.
"Are you here on official business? If not, even the president of your academy would need permission to enter. Those are the rules."
Chen Buhui let out a bitter laugh at the guard’s audacity.
"Fine. What a Luo Yao, what a Lin Ran, what a Luo Corporation—so arrogant in China, showing zero respect for their elders."
"Let’s see if you actually dare lay a hand on me."
Liu, her assistant, looked uneasy. "Ms. Chen, maybe we should just leave it."
"Leave it? If you’re spineless, go ahead and leave. What kind of young person has no fire in them? I’m going in."
With that, Chen Buhui stepped out of the car, ready to force her way through.
The guards tensed, poised to act.
At the critical moment, a voice came through the earpiece—Little Tong’s.
"Uncle Fu says she can come in now."
The guard exhaled quietly. He really hadn’t wanted to rough up an old lady.
"Our young lady is free now. You may enter."
Chen Buhui snorted.
"Hmph! Knew you wouldn’t dare stop me."
She climbed back into the car while the guard stayed silent, thinking to himself: If that call had come a few seconds later, you’d already be on the ground.
The other guards exchanged frowns.
"That’s Chen Buhui? She acts more like my elementary school teacher."
Meanwhile, inside the villa...
"Yao, Chen Buhui actually showed up. Interesting. What do you think she’s here for?"
Even Luo Yao couldn’t quite decipher Chen Buhui’s motives.
Given her official ties, visiting during such a sensitive period was... unusual.
During a government project bidding phase, a representative meeting privately with a competing company was already against protocol.
It was like the police, prosecutors, and judges jointly investigating a case—a big no-no. If no one followed the rules, chaos would reign.
Of course, Luo Yao was the exception. Rules didn’t apply to her.
"No idea."
Lin Ran wasn’t the sharpest, but he wasn’t stupid either. Yet he couldn’t figure out why Chen Buhui had come.
"She can’t seriously be here just to lecture us and leave. If so, I’d actually respect her for it."
Just then, the door swung open.
"Lin Ran, you’ve got some nerve, making an elder come to you like this?"
Lin Ran hadn’t expected Chen Buhui’s first words to be so confrontational—no greeting, nothing.
He frowned.
"Did I force you?"
If she wanted to be rude, he’d match her energy.
He’d been willing to show respect, but she clearly wasn’t interested.
Chen Buhui blinked, taken aback by Lin Ran’s sharp tone.
She then turned to Luo Yao.
"CEO Luo, let me clarify—I’m not here in any official capacity today."
Luo Yao nodded, "Naturally, if you were representing the authorities, I’d have sent you straight in for investigation."
Chen Buhui was taken aback again—he hadn’t expected Luo Yao to be so blunt either.
"Aren’t you going to invite me to sit?" Lin Ran gestured toward the sofa with his chin.
"You’re a grown adult. Is anyone stopping you?"
Chen Buhui’s face darkened slightly. After all these years, she had grown accustomed to being surrounded by flattery. Running into such disrespectful youngsters was a first for her.
"Fine. I won’t hold your lack of respect against you. After all, you don’t know who I am."
Lin Ran said, "I know you—Chen Buhui, one of the chief academicians at the Chinese Academy of Sciences."
Chen Buhui shook her head, glaring at Lin Ran in anger.
"To be precise, I’m your grandaunt."
Lin Ran replied, "I know."
"You know?"
"Yeah."
Chen Buhui let out a bitter laugh.
"If you knew I was your elder, how dare you treat me with such disrespect? You’ve been in Shanghai for days and didn’t even visit me. Young people these days have no sense of propriety."
Lin Ran glanced at Luo Yao, thinking to himself, Did I actually guess right?
"So, Grandaunt, what brings you here?"
"What brings me here? I’m here to teach you how to respect your elders. Not even your grandfather would dare treat me this way."
"No one has ever kept me waiting outside the door—you’re the first. No junior has ever failed to greet me properly—you’re the first. No one has ever—"
Lin Ran cut her off. "Hold on, hold on. No elder has ever dared to boss me around like this—you’re the first."

chapters.title: Chapter 348
chapters.content:
"Besides, we barely have any connection. That distant relative relationship is practically nonexistent in my eyes—so distant it might as well be non-existent. And yet you have the nerve to lecture me? Why don’t you just fly off into the sky?"
Though Chen Buhui was old, her reflexes were sharp. She immediately raised her voice.
"Distant? I’m your grandfather’s own sister. How is that distant?"
Lin Ran shrugged. "The only family I recognize is my wife. I suggest you tread carefully. If I really lose my temper, your heart might not be able to handle it."
Hearing Lin Ran’s words, Luo Yao’s eyes sparkled. She had stayed quiet ever since Chen Buhui entered the living room. But now, hearing Lin Ran declare that she was his only family, Luo Yao felt a wave of happiness.
"Arrogant! Is this how Chen Xiao raised you? You’re just as rebellious as your mother."
Lin Ran’s expression instantly turned icy as he fixed his gaze on Chen Buhui.
"What are you looking at? Am I wrong? Your mother, Chen Yanyan, defied her family to elope with some no-good man. And look how that turned out. Hmph."
Lin Ran narrowed his eyes.
"I won’t argue if you call Lin Tianba trash, but if you insult my mother—no. Right or wrong, she loved me. But you? You stand here pretending to be some elder, spewing venom. Out of respect for your past contributions to the nation, I’ll let it slide this time.""But if you say one more word, I won’t care if you’re old or a woman—I’ll hit you."
Lin Ran’s glare was terrifying. Even Chen Buhui felt a chill, hesitating.
Would this brat really hit an old woman?
Liu, the assistant, quickly stepped in to mediate.
"Ah, Elder Chen, didn’t you say you were just here to visit family? Why is everyone so tense? Young Master Lin, please don’t take it to heart. Elder Chen was just upset after being stopped by security earlier. We’re all family—no need for this."
She had only just learned about the connection between Chen Buhui and Lin Ran. No wonder the old woman had come.
Luo Yao, who had been silent until now, finally spoke. Her cold gaze swept over Chen Buhui.
"I don’t care if you’re from the Chen family or the Academy of Sciences. If you dare bully my husband in my home, do you think I’m just a decoration?"
Chen Buhui had crossed paths with Luo Yao before and knew about Luo Corporation’s collaborations with the government.
"Regardless, I’m Lin Ran’s elder, and as his wife, you’re my junior too. Isn’t it inappropriate to speak to me like this? Don’t think your little achievements and government ties give you the right to act however you want."
Luo Yao smirked dismissively.
"Oh? ‘Little achievements’? Do you know which company holds the highest honor in the scientific community? Do you know how many of your Academy’s projects are funded by me? Talk to me about achievements? You’re not even qualified."
"Don’t flatter yourself just because you’ve done a few things. Let me be blunt—your so-called ‘achievements’ are nothing in Luo Corporation’s eyes. And we both know how you got them."
Chen Buhui’s eyes widened in shock. The woman before her felt like an unfathomable abyss.
Just then—
"Miss, Young Master Lin, Chen Qingtian is here. Should we let her in?"
Lin Ran and Luo Yao exchanged glances.Thɪs
"Why is she here?"
Lin Ran knew Chen Qingtian was filming in the city, but he hadn’t invited her.
"No idea."
Luo Yao: "Let her in."
Chen Buhui, still reeling from Luo Yao’s words, grew even angrier when she saw Chen Qingtian waltz in effortlessly while she had been stopped at the door.
Cough. "It’s been a while since I’ve seen this girl. A perfectly decent young woman, and she chooses to become an actress. Who knows what kind of future she’ll have."
Lin Ran side-eyed Chen Buhui. Maybe it was time to show her the door.
"What era are you living in, calling her an ‘actress’ like it’s an insult? Stop pretending to be high and mighty."
"You—!"
Fine. She’d hold back. The situation wasn’t in her favor.
Soon, Chen Qingtian arrived. She ignored everyone else and went straight to Luo Yao.
"Little sister-in-law! I’m here! Did you miss me?"
Luo Yao: "No. Come or don’t come—I’d prefer if you didn’t."
Chen Qingtian: "..."
But embarrassment was a foreign concept to her.
"I heard you and my cousin were in town. I’ve been wanting to visit, but the crew wouldn’t give me time off. Today, my scenes wrapped up early, so here I am!"
She gave Luo Yao a pitiful look. "Little sister-in-law… do I still have a chance to get rich?"
Luo Yao: "Yes."
"How?"
"Go outside, find a luxury car, and crash into it. Then you’ll be rich."
Chen Qingtian: "Haha, since when did you learn to joke?"
Lin Ran chimed in.
"Maybe she’s serious. And you ignored me the second you walked in—went straight to my wife. Are you a lesbian or something?"
"Yao, stay away from her."
Luo Yao obediently took three steps back, eyeing Chen Qingtian thoughtfully.
Was she really a lesbian?
That’s disgusting.
Watching the younger generation banter so casually, Chen Buhui’s temper flared again.
"You’re all going too far! Have you forgotten I’m still here?"
Chen Qingtian turned, frowning in confusion.
"You are… Great-Aunt?"
"Obviously! Shouldn’t juniors greet their elders first when they arrive?"
Chen Qingtian rolled her eyes.
"Oh, sorry. Didn’t see you. My eyes only notice people I care about."
Chen Qingtian was infamous for her sharp tongue. Even if Chen Xiao himself were here, she wouldn’t hold back.
Truthfully, she had noticed Chen Buhui the moment she walked in—she just didn’t want to acknowledge her. Ugh, what terrible luck.
Back in their school days, Chen Buhui had been the most despised elder in the Chen family because of her endless lecturing.
Naturally, Chen Qingtian couldn’t stand her either.
"Didn’t see me? Young people these days pretend not to see their elders? Is this how your grandfather taught you to behave? Look at you—flaunting yourself on screen like some cheap—"
Chen Qingtian cut her off.
"Watch your mouth, or I’ll fire back. If you drop dead from anger on the way to the hospital, don’t blame me."
"If I’d known you were here, I wouldn’t have come. I’ve hated you since I was a kid. Running into you is the worst luck."
Chen Buhui pointed a trembling finger. "You—you insolent—!"
Chen Qingtian shrugged. "Old hag, say one more word, and I’ll pluck out every last one of your white hairs."
Liu, the assistant, nearly laughed out loud. Who knew the A-list actress had such savage comebacks?

chapters.title: Chapter 349
chapters.content:
Lin Ran shrugged and said to Chen Buhui,
"You see, everyone shares the same attitude toward you."
Chen Buhui finally couldn’t take it anymore.
"Fine, you two ungrateful brats just wait. And you, Luo Corporation—thinking you’ll get the tech city project? Keep dreaming."
Luo Yao: "Can you take responsibility for your words?"ᴛhis ᴜpdated by ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Why wouldn’t I?"
Luo Yao glanced at Uncle Fu.
"Extract this surveillance footage and send it to the authorities."
Chen Buhui froze on the spot, stunned by Luo Yao’s assertiveness.
"President Luo, I—I was just speaking out of anger earlier.""Can you communicate properly now?"
"Yes, yes."
"Who’s the ungrateful brat?"
"No one, I was just talking nonsense."
"Can you leave now?"
"I’ll go right away."
Chen Buhui left with Liu in tow, the latter utterly bewildered.
So, what was the point of coming here today?
Just to get humiliated?
After leaving, Chen Buhui remained silent the entire way.
"Professor Chen, don’t dwell on it. We’re in research—everything else is trivial."
Chen Buhui nodded. Upon returning to her residence, she made a phone call.
At the manor.
"Sis-in-law, thank you for driving that old hag away."
"I didn’t do it for you. It was for A’Ran."
Chen Qingtian: "..."
"Please, sis-in-law, teach me how to do business. I don’t want to act anymore."
Lin Ran: "???"
"Your boss is right here. If you want to break your contract, prepare the penalty fee first."
Chen Qingtian: "Dear cousin, my dreams are priceless. You wouldn’t crush them with money, would you?"
Lin Ran was both amused and exasperated. He’d always suspected Chen Qingtian’s brain worked differently—her logic was anything but ordinary.
Her language could be crude, but her blunt, carefree personality made it hard to dislike her.
"My wife hates people who can’t commit. A fickle woman like you trying to corrupt her? Get out of here."
Chen Qingtian didn’t budge, staring pitifully at the couple.
Luo Yao: "Want to make money?"
"Yes."
"Fine. I’ll set up a film company for you under Nuan Yao Media. You’ll be the CEO while keeping your current career."
Chen Qingtian’s eyes instantly lit up. "Really?"
Lin Ran: "???"
Luo Yao nodded.
"Really. And you can recruit all the pretty girls from Nuan Yao Media as your talent pool. Pick the most capable and attractive ones—packaging celebrities doesn’t require much skill. With enough capital backing, even a pig could succeed."
Chen Qingtian suddenly felt life was worth living again.
"Sis-in-law, you’re my savior. But let me clarify—I may be a star, but I’m not a pig."
She nearly dropped to her knees in gratitude.
Could she start her own company? Of course.
But having a corporate giant as a springboard was a whole different game.
Chen Qingtian was already fantasizing about hiring a bunch of young, handsome actors. Sitting in her office, coaching a different pretty boy every day—what a life.
Glancing around the manor, she imagined owning a mansion like this someday.
"This villa is huge. Can I pick a room to rest in?"
With Luo Yao’s permission, Chen Qingtian practically skipped with joy. If Wu Zhishang didn’t summon her back, she might stay in Shanghai for a long time.
At dinner, Chen Qingtian chattered nonstop like a songbird.
"Wow, sis-in-law, this food is amazing. You have no idea what I’ve endured in Shanghai—those crew meals are inedible. But I have to eat them, or people will accuse me of being a diva."
"Being a star seems glamorous, but the hardships? Unimaginable. I’m lucky—my background protects me. Other women trying to stay ‘untainted’ in this industry? A pipe dream."
The more she talked, the more animated she became. As a celebrity, her stories naturally revolved around showbiz.
"Our assistant director is a tyrant—yells at people like they’re dogs. Worse, he ‘discusses scripts’ with actresses at midnight. Thank goodness I’m a Chen—he wouldn’t dare touch me."
"But sis-in-law, you’re incredible. Our whole crew was buzzing about you exposing the Li family. Even I didn’t know the industry could be this explosive..."
Lin Ran finally set down his chopsticks.
"Cousin, we don’t have a ‘no talking at meals’ rule, but you’re overdoing it."
Chen Qingtian muttered, "I’m just talking. You..."
Suddenly, she froze. Lin Ran had just peeled a shrimp, fed it to Luo Yao, then wiped the corner of her mouth with his finger.
"Ugh, what kind of couple cruelty—no, single-beauty cruelty is this?"
Lin Ran’s gaze stayed on Luo Yao as he replied,
"You, a manless single woman, dreaming of raising ten or eight toy boys? Show me one first, then talk."
Chen Qingtian: "..."
That hurt.
"So men can be this devoted? Suddenly, ten or eight isn’t enough—I need more who love me like this."
Luo Yao / Lin Ran: "..."
Lin Ran: "How delusional. You think you deserve love?"
Chen Qingtian said earnestly, "Of course. I may want many lovers, but I’m not a heartbreaker—I just want to give them all a home."
Lin Ran’s face darkened. "Hah... well, I hope your dream comes true. But stay away from my wife."
"Afraid I’ll corrupt her?"
"Afraid she’ll kill you."
Chen Qingtian corrupting Luo Yao? A pipe dream.
Luo Yao was a textbook yandere—obsessed with Lin Ran alone.
Luo Yao gazed at Lin Ran with adoration, her eyes full of longing. She needed an outlet.
"A’Ran, let’s rest early."
"Okay."
Chen Qingtian mumbled between bites, "So early? What’s wrong with you?"
The nearby maids blushed.
The young mistress could be... loud.
"A’Ran, I... I want..." Luo Yao suddenly bit Lin Ran’s shoulder, as if his blood nourished her.
Moonlight drapes silken gowns, $2hispers sweet in tender sounds.
Strings in harmony entwine, $2ovebirds dream in sheets divine.
What poetry.
Late at night, too excited to sleep in such luxury, Chen Qingtian sneaked out alone.
Not wanting to disturb anyone, she wandered outside to admire the manor’s nightscape.
Even the round-the-clock staff didn’t notice her leaving.
